The Oscar-winner, 87, will join a cast including Charlie Plummer, Stephen Graham, Toni Collette, Isabela Merced and Maisy Stella in Ibelin, director Morten Tyldum’s new drama. The film, directed by Oscar nominee Mortem – best known for The Imitation Game – is based on the real-life story of Mats Steen, a Norwegian man with a degenerative muscular disease who lived much of his social and emotional life through the online game. Its title comes from Mats’ virtual alter ego in World of Warcraft. Written by BAFTA nominee Ilaria Bernardini and Oscar-nominated screenwriter Hossein Amini, Ibelin draws from Mats’ blog Musings of Life. The film explores both the World of Warcraft community that came to admire Steen and his loving but chaotic family, who discovered the depth of his virtual world only after his death. Vendôme Pictures and Pathé are reuniting to produce the film, following their previous collaboration on the Oscar-winning CODA. Vendôme’s Philippe Rousselet and Fabrice Gianfermi will produce alongside Jérôme Seydoux at Pathé and Tyldum and Guri Neby for Neby-Tyldum AS. Vendôme and Pathé are financing the production, with Black Bear handling international sales and CAA Media Finance representing domestic rights ahead of the American Film Market in Los Angeles. Principal photography is set to begin in Europe in 2026. Charlie Plummer, who recently appeared in Francis Lawrence’s The Long Walk, brings experience from films such as All the Money in the World and Lean on Pete. Stephen Graham, who recently won three Emmys for creating and starring in the Netflix hit Adolescence, has also featured in Springsteen: Deliver Me from Nowhere, The Irishman and Rocketman. Toni Collette, currently starring in Netflix’s Wayward, is known for Hereditary, Knives Out and her Oscar-nominated role in The Sixth Sense. And Isabela Merced, who stars in The Last of Us and plays Hawkgirl in Superman, joins Maisy Stella, who recently led My Old A** and will star in Maude Apatow’s upcoming feature Poetic License. Sir Anthony, a two-time Oscar winner for The Silence of the Lambs and dementia drama The Father, brings his trademark intensity to the ensemble after his acclaimed performances in Remains of the Day, Howard’s End and The Two Popes have cemented his status as one of cinema’s most respected icons. Now, we have a closer look at the creature's design... News By JoshWilding - Nov 21, 2025 01:11 PM EST Filed Under: Superman When James Gunn shared a first look at Superman , everyone was eager to know what that glowing orb in the sky was. Could it be Parasite? Mongul's spaceship? An interdimensional portal? As the speculation continued, the expectation was that the orb might be tied to the movie's big bad. Nope. In reality, the Fifth-Dimensional Imp just appeared in the background of a scene featuring Clark Kent and Lois Lane. Shortly after Superman 's release, Gunn was asked if it could be Mister Mxyzptlk, and replied, "Oh, no. He’s just a stupid basic imp. He’s nowhere near as powerful as Mister Mxyzptlk." While it may not have been that iconic member of Superman's rogues gallery, the fact that Imps like this one are causing chaos in the DCU promises to be very exciting for this franchise's future. Today, artist Adam Milicevic has shared his final designs for the unnamed Imp introduced in Superman . On his website , he wrote, "Final Concept and Design for the Inter-dimensional Imp as seen in Superman. Done for Legacy Effects. Lots of iterations on this jelly boi." Mister Mxyzptlk first appeared in 1944's Superman #30 , and is a Fifth-Dimensional Imp from the land of Zrfff. He possesses near-omnipotent reality-warping powers and is limited only by his inability to refuse a challenge to say, spell, or write his name backwards, which banishes him to the fifth dimension for at least 90 days. Only time will tell whether Gunn brings Mister Mxyzptlk into the DCU. For now, the filmmaker is concentrating on Brainiac in Man of Tomorrow , a movie that stars David Corenswet as Clark Kent/Superman, Nicholas Hoult as Lex Luthor, Rachel Brosnahan as Lois Lane, Isabela Merced as Kendra Saunders/Hawkgirl, and Frank Grillo as Rick Flag, Sr. Several actors and characters are rumoured to appear, including Aaron Pierre's John Stewart/Green Lantern and John Cena's Peacemaker. Gunn has repeatedly said he'd like to introduce another Imp, Bat-Mite, but it's hard to say when and where he'll be able to make that a reality. "Superman is an indescribable joy," we said in our review . "A beautiful, moving thrill, David Corenswet is the perfect Man of Steel in a movie packed full of ideas. Fortunately, under James Gunn’s expert direction, all of those work, creating a rousing experience that flies higher than DC has in a very long time." Pictures Movies Superman: DCU Movie Set Photos Include a Funny Easter Egg November 19, 2025 By Evolve Editors Some new Superman set photos reveal a surprising connection shared between the titular DCU superhero and a villainous character. DC Studios and Warner Bros. Pictures ’ Superman was released in United States theaters this past July. Directed by James Gunn , the movie stars David Corenswet as the Man of Steel, Nicholas Hoult as Lex Luthor, and Rachel Brosnahan as Lois Lane. A follow-up movie, titled Man of Tomorrow , is now in development and is dated for 2027. What do we see in the Superman set photos? On Threads , Gunn shared some behind-the-scenes photos taken from the set of Superman. More specifically, the photos were taken on the Moravian Palace set, which is where Zlatko Burić’s Vasil Ghurkos character resides. The photos noticeably feature images of squirrels, which is relevant because there’s a scene elsewhere in Superman where Kal-El saves a squirrel from being crushed. Thus, it appears that both Clark Kent and Vasil Ghurkos are big fans of the furry little creatures. View a screenshot of Gunn’s post below: Photo Credit: James Gunn on Threads The synopsis for Superman reads, “Superman, DC Studios’ first feature film to hit the big screen, is set to soar into theaters worldwide this summer from Warner Bros. Pictures. In his signature style, James Gunn takes on the original superhero in the newly imagined DC universe with a singular blend of epic action, humor, and heart, delivering a Superman who’s driven by compassion and an inherent belief in the goodness of humankind.” The cast of the movie further includes Edi Gathegi as Michael Holt/Mister Terrific, Anthony Carrigan as Rex Mason/Metamorpho, Nathan Fillion as Guy Gardner/Green Lantern, Isabela Merced as Kendra Saunders/Hawkgirl, Skyler Gisondo as Jimmy Olsen, Wendell Pierce as Perry White, Mikaela Hoover as Cat Grant, Beck Bennett as Steve Lombard, Christopher McDonald as Ron Troupe, and more. Superman is now available to stream on HBO Max. Man of Tomorrow will be released in theaters on July 9, 2027. Originally reported by Brandon Schreur at SuperHeroHype . We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy. 2 min read On Friday night, Nicky Zimmermann and Simone Zimmermann hosted a star-studded dinner at Chateau Marmont to celebrate the Australian brand’s cruise 2026 collection, “Twisted Romance.” The new collection is inspired by “nostalgia, femininity, and the fantasy of escape,” and the glamorous celebration reflected the same feeling. Guests, including Zoey Deutch, Jurnee Smollett, and Emma Roberts, were treated to a candlelit dinner in the famed hotel’s Bungalow, at tables set with antique candelabras, strings of pearls, and lush greenery. Stefanie Keenan // Getty Images Emma Roberts before dinner. Following dinner, guests headed upstairs to the Chateau Marmont’s Penthouse for dancing and continued festivities, complete with a set by DJ Kitty Kash. WWD // Getty Images DJ Kitty Kash manning the turntable. “Cruise 26 is inspired by nostalgic pirate adventures and the flamboyance of the New Romantics,” said Nicky in a statement on the new collection. “A treasure trove of nostalgia is given fresh interpretation through fluid fabrics, dynamic shapes and illustrative prints to capture a carefree mood.” The creative director continued, “We played a lot with contrast—floaty silks against structured denim, delicate lace paired with sharp tailoring. There’s volume, romance, and drama, but it’s never too serious. That tension is what makes it feel modern: celebrating a sense of fun, freedom and a little rebellious adventure.” Stefanie Keenan // Getty Images Nina Garcia and Bella Heathcote. The invite list included some of the biggest names in Hollywood, all of them wearing pieces from the collection, including Dakota Fanning, Rita Ora, Halle Bailey, Delaney Rowe, Isabela Merced, Bella Heathcote, Maria Bakalova, Abby Champion, and more. ELLE’s editor-in-chief Nina Garcia was also in attendance. Scroll through the gallery below for a glimpse inside the evening. By Joe Anderton Published: 08 November 2025 Stephen Graham has had a busy 2025, appearing in A Thousand Blows , Springsteen: Deliver Me From Nowhere , and a little-known show called Adolescence . But he isn't slowing down – far from it in fact. The prolific actor has been confirmed as one of the cast members for Ibelin , the real-life story of a Norwegian man named Mats Steen. Steen suffered from degenerative muscle disease which severely limited his ability to participate in every day activities. Instead, he decided to pour most of his time and effort into his World of Warcraft character, the titular Ibelin. What to Read Next He also kept a blog where he documented his life living with the condition, known as Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Following his passing, he became a legend in the game's community, and was honoured with a gravestone within the virtual realm by creators Blizzard. Marc Piasecki // Getty Images Related: UK film release dates As reported by Variety , Graham has been confirmed for the "inspirational" film, alongside Sir Anthony Hopkins, Charlie Plummer, Toni Collette, Isabela Merced, and Maisy Stella. The Imitation Game 's Morten Tyldum is directing the movie, which is based on a script from Ilaria Bernardini and Hossein Amini. The film is set to explore both Steen's family, as well as the World of Warcraft players who became fans of Steen and his digital alter-ego. Steen's story was previously immortalised in the Netflix documentary The Remarkable Life of Ibelin , which was released in October 2024. The film used real-life text logs from Ibelin's guild, as well as character models and other assets from World of Warcraft , to tell its story It was highly acclaimed, sitting at a near-perfect 97% positive score on Rotten Tomatoes from 60 critic reviews. Kevin Mazur // Getty Images Related: Quentin Tarantino's two-part "masterpiece" Kill Bill is getting epic new release with unseen footage Meanwhile, Graham is set to continue to explore the themes included in Adolescence through the book Letters to Our Sons . "After the huge impact of Adolescence , I realised there was a greater need for communication between fathers and sons," the actor said. "There is arguably an even bigger disconnect than ever before. "I would love to help create more opportunity for fathers to reach out to their sons and carry on the conversation." The new edition of Living Legends is here! Buy Ariana & Witches in newsagents or online , priced at just £8.99. Joe Anderton Joe Anderton is a freelance news writer at Digital Spy , having worked there since 2016. In his time, he's covered a host of live events and interviewed celebrities big and small. A big fan of TV and movies both mainstream and obscure, Joe also enjoys video games and in particular PlayStation. Joe currently does not use Twitter, but he only ever used it to tell people to watch the film Help! I'm a Fish . In 2018, Sheridan returned to the world of Sicario with Sicario: Day of the Soldado , the action sequel starring Josh Brolin and Benicio del Toro . The film continues the story of the escalating drug war between the U.S. and Mexico. In America, Sicario: Day of the Soldado is streaming exclusively on Starz , but globally, the film recently hit Netflix, where it’s charting in the top 10 in more than 10 countries around the world. Sicario: Day of the Soldado came at a time when movies didn’t cost quite as much to make as they do now. The movie cost Lionsgate only $35 million to produce, meaning that its $75 million box office total was enough for it to turn a profit. The film earned mediocre and forgettable scores of 62% from critics and 66% from audiences, which fall well below the 91% and 85% scores held by its predecessor. Emily Blunt and Daniel Kaluuya did not return for Sicario 2 , but the film did cast Isabela Merced in a leading role. After sci-fi savant Denis Villeneuve directed the first Sicario from Sheridan’s script, Lionsgate recruited Stefano Sollima to direct the sequel. Sheridan has confirmed publicly that the studio wasn’t happy with his creative process on the movie , which came as a result of his reclusive behavior when writing the script. Sheridan told the executives he was going home to his ranch in Texas to write the movie, and he’d hand in his final draft when he was ready. Taylor Sheridan Is Working on Another Sicario Movie Fans have been waiting for a third Sicario movie for years, and Josh Brolin recently confirmed that Sheridan is writing the script for another installment in the franchise. He let this spill while on the press tour for his new horror hit, Weapons , which is now streaming on HBO Max. It may be a while before Sheridan gets to a place where he can prioritize Sicario 3 , though. He’s hard at work on a new action movie, F.A.S.T. , and he’s been tapped to write the script for the Call of Duty movie in the works at Paramount. Be sure to watch Sicario: Day of the Soldado on Starz in America or Netflix globally and stay tuned to Collider for more streaming updates. Celebrities , Entertainment Oct 28, 2025 “Grotesque”: People Are Reacting Strongly to Cynthia Erivo’s Controversial Harper’s Bazaar Shoot Abel Musa Miño Entertainment News Writer 15 8 15 Link copied! Share Link copied! Share ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Cynthia Erivo ’s Harper’s Bazaar cover was meant to celebrate artistry and self-expression. But instead of admiration, the photos provoked a wave of disgust . The 38-year-old Wicked star posed bare for the magazine’s November issue, wearing nothing but sheer black tights and heels. Other looks included a white sheer gown with silver detailing, a plunging black dress, a dramatic ruffled ensemble, and finally, a gold bodysuit paired with a full-face mask. Highlights Cynthia Erivo’s Harper’s Bazaar shoot was praised by some as daring, and slammed by others as “grotesque.” Fans of glamour and fashion called it “refreshing,” praising her presence and artistic range Erivo spoke about how Jada Plinkett Smith helped her navigate fame and “recognize her power.” Mainstream outlets described the shoot with words like “sensational,” “incredible,” and “head-turning.” But online, the tone was anything but . “ Harper’s Bizarre fits better,” one user wrote. “She looks like Nosferatu,” another added. RELATED: Cynthia Erivo’s latest magazine cover ignited a debate online with detractors labeling her a “narcissistic mess” Cynthia Erivo posing in a striking black outfit on Harper’s Bazaar cover, sparking strong reactions to the grotesque shoot. Image credits: Harper’s Bazaar/Cass Bird ADVERTISEMENT Even among those who value Erivo’s talent the reactions were negative . “She has an incredible voice, her style on the red carpet has been faultless, but these pictures cheapen all that,” one reader said. “It’s unnecessary.” “I don’t get these pictures. They do her no favors,” another replied. Others were much harsher in their assessment, labeling Erivo as a “narcissistic mess,” and her now signature style — defined by her shaved head and gaunt frame — as unsettling rather than empowering. “I won’t be buying this issue,” a reader stated. “She looks grotesque . I would run if I saw her.” Cynthia Erivo posing in a sheer, intricate gown in a Harper's Bazaar shoot sparking grotesque reactions online. Image credits: Harper’s Bazaar/Cass Bird Many mocked the elaborate and sharp acrylic nails, one of Erivo’s signature accessories, shown in several shots. “Those nails must cause a few injuries,” a user commented. “How does someone wipe their backside properly with nails like that?” ADVERTISEMENT What was framed by Bazaar as a high-fashion exploration of identity came across to some viewers as ultimately self-indulgent. “She’s exhausting ,” a reader wrote. Over the years, netizens have reacted to Erivo with a mix of admiration for her talent, and frustration with her behavior Cynthia Erivo posing topless with tattoos and jewelry in a striking and controversial Harper’s Bazaar fashion shoot. Image credits: Harper’s Bazaar/Cass Bird The backlash didn’t come in a vacuum. Erivo’s public image has been declining for over a year, caught between feelings of admiration and annoyance. First during the Wicked promotional tour, and again this year after her controversial casting as Jesus Christ in Jesus Christ Superstar . Cynthia Erivo posing in sheer black tights and heels with tattoos and jewelry in controversial Harper’s Bazaar shoot. Image credits: Harper’s Bazaar/Cass Bird ADVERTISEMENT While her talent was rarely questioned by netizens, her behavior off-camera earned her a reputation for arrogance. Reports of her disparaging fellow actresses, snapping at interviewers, and complaining about “being othered” despite her success led some to see her as detached from reality. Cynthia Erivo posing in a sculptural black dress with a gold belt, striking an expressive pose in a high-fashion shoot. Image credits: Harper’s Bazaar/Cass Bird “Doesn’t she realize how utterly absurd this perpetual-victim schtick sounds coming from people that have reached the pinnacle of their craft?” a reader wrote last year. So when she appeared on stage as Jesus, for many the ultimate symbol of humility, some found it hypocritical . “In reverse it would be cultural and gender appropriation! Hollywood should be ashamed,” a viewer said at the time. Erivo has been widely recognized as one of the most talented and successful actresses in Hollywood ADVERTISEMENT Two women posing together at an event, reflecting the strong reactions to Cynthia Erivo’s controversial Harper’s Bazaar shoot. Image credits: Getty/Alberto Rodriguez Erivo’s supporters, on the other hand, see in her a symbol of endurance and power. They see a woman of color rising through the ranks to become one of the most respected artists in the world and the current Vice President of the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, her alma mater. As both an actress and singer, Erivo is one of the few individuals in history nominated for a Grammy, an Oscar, a Tony Award, and an Emmy. Cynthia Erivo wearing a black textured jacket and smiling during a discussion about the controversial Harper’s Bazaar shoot. Image credits: Instagram/cynthiaerivo ADVERTISEMENT Despite her accomplishments, Erivo has developed a public image shaped by what many see as a contradiction in how she presents herself. To critics, she’s someone who positions herself as both a victim and an icon, constantly lecturing audiences while insisting she’s misunderstood. That tension has made her a polarizing figure. Netizens often describe feeling “talked down to” by her interviews and speeches. “She acts like she’s both oppressed and superior,” one commenter wrote. Cynthia Erivo in a black dress and another woman in white, attending an event with guests and photographers in the background. Image credits: Getty/Dave Benett The perception isn’t new. Back in 2013, Erivo angered a segment of the African American community after mocking their accent on social media. “She cannot stand black Americans, we are ghetto, low life, and lazy! But has all the audacity to play our historical figures,” a reader wrote at the time. Fashion fans were delighted by the photoshoot, and praised the actress’ expressions Cynthia Erivo in floral patterned coat dress and matching bag posing for controversial Harper’s Bazaar shoot outdoors. Image credits: Harper’s Bazaar/Cass Bird In her Harper’s Bazaar interview, Erivo said she feels “fully myself right now,” crediting friend Jada Pinkett Smith for guiding her through fame. “Recognize the beauty and the power that you possess,” Jada told her. While certain parts of the internet recoiled at the shoot, fashion and glamour fans praised it as one of the most visually interesting celebrity editorials they had seen. “I just love her silhouette,” one fan wrote, as another called the spread “the most interesting celeb shoot I’ve seen in a while.” Others focused on details such as her tattoos and physique. “Her thigh tattoos are amazing,” one fan wrote. “I am always baffled that such a petite woman can look so statuesque,” another added. “I think she’s the only person I have ever seen that can do this.” Even some of her detractors turned around to praise her. “ Cynthia can do and say whatever she wants, quite frankly. If I had half the talent she does I would be insufferable .” “Weirder and weirder.” Netizens took to social media to share their thoughts on the photos Social media reactions to Cynthia Erivo’s controversial Harper’s Bazaar shoot labeled grotesque by many viewers. Celebrities , Entertainment Oct 28, 2025 “Grotesque”: People Are Reacting Strongly to Cynthia Erivo’s Controversial Harper’s Bazaar Shoot Abel Musa Miño Entertainment News Writer 15 8 15 Link copied! Share Link copied! Share ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Cynthia Erivo ’s Harper’s Bazaar cover was meant to celebrate artistry and self-expression. But instead of admiration, the photos provoked a wave of disgust . The 38-year-old Wicked star posed bare for the magazine’s November issue, wearing nothing but sheer black tights and heels. Other looks included a white sheer gown with silver detailing, a plunging black dress, a dramatic ruffled ensemble, and finally, a gold bodysuit paired with a full-face mask. Highlights Cynthia Erivo’s Harper’s Bazaar shoot was praised by some as daring, and slammed by others as “grotesque.” Fans of glamour and fashion called it “refreshing,” praising her presence and artistic range Erivo spoke about how Jada Plinkett Smith helped her navigate fame and “recognize her power.” Mainstream outlets described the shoot with words like “sensational,” “incredible,” and “head-turning.” But online, the tone was anything but . “ Harper’s Bizarre fits better,” one user wrote. “She looks like Nosferatu,” another added. RELATED: Cynthia Erivo’s latest magazine cover ignited a debate online with detractors labeling her a “narcissistic mess” Cynthia Erivo posing in a striking black outfit on Harper’s Bazaar cover, sparking strong reactions to the grotesque shoot. Image credits: Harper’s Bazaar/Cass Bird ADVERTISEMENT Even among those who value Erivo’s talent the reactions were negative . “She has an incredible voice, her style on the red carpet has been faultless, but these pictures cheapen all that,” one reader said. “It’s unnecessary.” “I don’t get these pictures. They do her no favors,” another replied. Others were much harsher in their assessment, labeling Erivo as a “narcissistic mess,” and her now signature style — defined by her shaved head and gaunt frame — as unsettling rather than empowering. “I won’t be buying this issue,” a reader stated. “She looks grotesque . I would run if I saw her.” Cynthia Erivo posing in a sheer, intricate gown in a Harper's Bazaar shoot sparking grotesque reactions online. Image credits: Harper’s Bazaar/Cass Bird Many mocked the elaborate and sharp acrylic nails, one of Erivo’s signature accessories, shown in several shots. “Those nails must cause a few injuries,” a user commented. “How does someone wipe their backside properly with nails like that?” ADVERTISEMENT What was framed by Bazaar as a high-fashion exploration of identity came across to some viewers as ultimately self-indulgent. “She’s exhausting ,” a reader wrote. Over the years, netizens have reacted to Erivo with a mix of admiration for her talent, and frustration with her behavior Cynthia Erivo posing topless with tattoos and jewelry in a striking and controversial Harper’s Bazaar fashion shoot. Image credits: Harper’s Bazaar/Cass Bird The backlash didn’t come in a vacuum. Erivo’s public image has been declining for over a year, caught between feelings of admiration and annoyance. First during the Wicked promotional tour, and again this year after her controversial casting as Jesus Christ in Jesus Christ Superstar . Cynthia Erivo posing in sheer black tights and heels with tattoos and jewelry in controversial Harper’s Bazaar shoot. Image credits: Harper’s Bazaar/Cass Bird ADVERTISEMENT While her talent was rarely questioned by netizens, her behavior off-camera earned her a reputation for arrogance. Reports of her disparaging fellow actresses, snapping at interviewers, and complaining about “being othered” despite her success led some to see her as detached from reality. Cynthia Erivo posing in a sculptural black dress with a gold belt, striking an expressive pose in a high-fashion shoot. Image credits: Harper’s Bazaar/Cass Bird “Doesn’t she realize how utterly absurd this perpetual-victim schtick sounds coming from people that have reached the pinnacle of their craft?” a reader wrote last year. So when she appeared on stage as Jesus, for many the ultimate symbol of humility, some found it hypocritical . “In reverse it would be cultural and gender appropriation! Hollywood should be ashamed,” a viewer said at the time. Erivo has been widely recognized as one of the most talented and successful actresses in Hollywood ADVERTISEMENT Two women posing together at an event, reflecting the strong reactions to Cynthia Erivo’s controversial Harper’s Bazaar shoot. Image credits: Getty/Alberto Rodriguez Erivo’s supporters, on the other hand, see in her a symbol of endurance and power. They see a woman of color rising through the ranks to become one of the most respected artists in the world and the current Vice President of the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, her alma mater. As both an actress and singer, Erivo is one of the few individuals in history nominated for a Grammy, an Oscar, a Tony Award, and an Emmy. Cynthia Erivo wearing a black textured jacket and smiling during a discussion about the controversial Harper’s Bazaar shoot. Image credits: Instagram/cynthiaerivo ADVERTISEMENT Despite her accomplishments, Erivo has developed a public image shaped by what many see as a contradiction in how she presents herself. To critics, she’s someone who positions herself as both a victim and an icon, constantly lecturing audiences while insisting she’s misunderstood. That tension has made her a polarizing figure. Netizens often describe feeling “talked down to” by her interviews and speeches. “She acts like she’s both oppressed and superior,” one commenter wrote. Cynthia Erivo in a black dress and another woman in white, attending an event with guests and photographers in the background. Image credits: Getty/Dave Benett The perception isn’t new. Back in 2013, Erivo angered a segment of the African American community after mocking their accent on social media. “She cannot stand black Americans, we are ghetto, low life, and lazy! But has all the audacity to play our historical figures,” a reader wrote at the time. Fashion fans were delighted by the photoshoot, and praised the actress’ expressions Cynthia Erivo in floral patterned coat dress and matching bag posing for controversial Harper’s Bazaar shoot outdoors. Image credits: Harper’s Bazaar/Cass Bird In her Harper’s Bazaar interview, Erivo said she feels “fully myself right now,” crediting friend Jada Pinkett Smith for guiding her through fame. “Recognize the beauty and the power that you possess,” Jada told her. While certain parts of the internet recoiled at the shoot, fashion and glamour fans praised it as one of the most visually interesting celebrity editorials they had seen. “I just love her silhouette,” one fan wrote, as another called the spread “the most interesting celeb shoot I’ve seen in a while.” Others focused on details such as her tattoos and physique. “Her thigh tattoos are amazing,” one fan wrote. “I am always baffled that such a petite woman can look so statuesque,” another added. “I think she’s the only person I have ever seen that can do this.” Even some of her detractors turned around to praise her. “ Cynthia can do and say whatever she wants, quite frankly. If I had half the talent she does I would be insufferable .” “Weirder and weirder.” Netizens took to social media to share their thoughts on the photos Social media reactions to Cynthia Erivo’s controversial Harper’s Bazaar shoot labeled grotesque by many viewers. By George Lewis Published: 28 October 2025 As one of the most highly-anticipated films of the year, Wicked: For Good has a lot of hype to live up to. With its release now under a month away, it seems that fans will be delighted if the first reactions are anything to go by. The upcoming musical fantasy will continue the stories of Elphaba (Cynthia Erivo) and Glinda (Ariana Grande) following their emotional separation at the end of the first film, with Elphaba continuing to be cast as a villain in the magical world of Oz. Directed by Jon M Chu once again, Wicked: For Good boasts a stacked supporting cast including Jonathan Bailey, Jeff Goldblum, Michelle Yeoh and Marissa Bode, with the film hoping to replicate the commercial and critical success of its predecessor. What to Read Next While we'll have to wait to see how it performs at the box office, it seems that critics are once again wowed by the musical extravaganza, with the early reactions being incredibly positive thus far. "Get ready because #WickedForGood exceeds all expectations," wrote Jazz Tangcay of Variety on X . "Jon M Chu is a genius in the way he brings this to a close. Elphaba and Glinda’s stories are expanded, and leave you with an emotional gut punch at the end." Universal Related: Best streaming services UK 2025 — including Disney Plus, Netflix, iPlayer and Apple TV+ "Cynthia Erivo is magnificent, but get ready for Ariana Grande as she takes this performance to the next level," they continued as they described her role as a "tour de force". "And wow, the world building, the costumes, and Alice Brooks cinematography deserve your attention. Can not wait to see it again. I sobbed hard. Wicked: For Good is sheer musical greatness." Ada Enechi of BuzzFeed and Channel 4 was similarly full of praise as they posted on X , writing: "Embargo up? #WickedForGood delivers in every way possible. The new original songs…life changing!" "They will melt your heart in ways you can’t even imagine. Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande have cemented their places in history, this is truly an unmissable sequel," they continued. Universal Related: "What a legend!": Wicked 2 reveals surprise Netflix star voicing the Cowardly Lion "#WickedForGood flies high. Jon M Chu helms an emotionally timely piece that deepens every spell cast by the first film. No surprise, Cynthia Erivo & Ariana Grande are SPECTACULAR (again)... A heartfelt end to Oz’s greatest friendship," wrote Variety 's Clayton Davis. Deadline also lauded the film earlier this month , writing: "Whatever spell Chu used, it worked because Wicked: For Good works for good on so many levels. Some might even argue that it's a tighter, more thrilling, more exciting film than Wicked ." Wicked: For Good is released in cinemas on 21 November. The new edition of Living Legends is here! His film tastes vary from blockbusters like Mission: Impossible and John Wick to international directors such as Paolo Sorrentino and Hirokazu Kore-eda, and has attended both the London and Berlin film festivals. The actor, 87, shut down rumors that he and his “The Silence of the Lambs” co-star, Jodie Foster, were feuding while making the 1991 classic. “I met Jodie, and she was very nice,” Hopkins recalled while on the “Armchair Expert” podcast . “There’s quotes that Jodie never spoke to me. That’s not true. We were quite friendly. There’s nothing spooky about it. That’s publicly crap.” 7 Anthony Hopkins and Jodie Foster in “The Silence of the Lambs” in 1991. ©Orion Pictures Corp/Courtesy Everett Co / Everett Collection In the star’s new book “We Did OK, Kid: A Memoir,” he wrote that he and Foster, 62, mostly stayed away from each other while filming because of their characters. Hopkins portrayed Hannibal Lecter, a cannibalistic murderer, while the actress played Clarice Starling an FBI agent in training, trying to get info out of him about another serial killer. Starling was meant to be intimidated by Lecter. Explore More Katy Perry sues dying veteran, 85, for $5M Jenny McCarthy reveals scary health struggles that caused growth in eyes, teeth to fall out Sydney Sweeney shows off her curves in plunging white swimsuit during holiday with Scooter Braun Hopkins told host Dax Shepard, 50, that Foster was impressed with his performance. “We did the first reading, and I knew how to play it,” he recounted. “It was the first reading around a table in New York, of all places. So we finished the script and Kenny Utt, one of the producers, says, ‘Holy Moses, Tony, what is that?’ And Jodie said, ‘You’re scary.'” Hopkins further detailed the moment in his new memoir. 7 Jodie Foster in “The Silence of the Lambs.” ©Orion Pictures Corp/Courtesy Everett Co / Everett Collection “We just flew right into it,” he penned. “I wanted to show what I could do, so I was as scary as I could be. You could have heard a pin drop in the room. A couple of seconds after I started to speak as Lecter, I saw Jodie grow tense.” The film took home five Oscars in 1992, with Hopkins landing the award for Best Actor and Foster winning for Best Actress. The project also scored an Oscar for Best Director, Best Adapted Screenplay, and Best Picture. Hopkins also wrote about having lunch with Foster on the last day of filming. “Jodie put down her sandwich and said she had to confess something: she’d been scared of me,” he elaborated. Hopkins added that he felt the same way towards her. “We had a big hug, and we both admitted to feeling a strange sense of distance during the shoot, due no doubt to the power of that script, which had us playing a cat-and-mouse game,” he continued. “Since then, we’ve always greeted each other with great warmth.” 7 Anthony Hopkins in the 1991 horror film. ©Orion Pictures Corp/Courtesy Everett Co / Everett Collection 7 Anthony Hopkins as the iconic Hannibal Lecter. ©Orion Pictures Corp/Courtesy Everett Collection Hopkins’ podcast appearance comes on the heels of him disputing his wife Stella Arroyave’s belief that he has autism. “I’m obsessed with numbers. I’m obsessed with detail. I like everything in order. And memorizing,” the “Hannibal” alum told the Sunday Times earlier this month. “Stella looked it up and she said, ‘You must be Asperger’s,’” he said about his wife of over 20 years. “I didn’t know what the hell she was talking about,” Hopkins continued. “I don’t even believe it.” 7 Anthony Hopkins with wife Stella Arroyave during 2005 Venice Film Festival. WireImage Asperger’s Syndrome now falls under the broader umbrella of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), according to the Cleveland Clinic . ASD, per the Mayo Clinic , is a condition related to brain development that affects how people see others and socialize with them. Hopkins went on to share his perspective on mental health labels. “Well, I guess I’m cynical because it’s all nonsense,” he expressed. “It’s all rubbish. ADHD, OCD, Asperger’s, blah, blah, blah. Oh God, it’s called living.” 7 Stella Arroyave and Sir Anthony Hopkins on January 17, 2025 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Getty Images for GEA “It’s just being a human being, full of tangled webs and mysteries and stuff that’s in us,” Hopkins added. “Full of warts and grime and craziness, it’s the human condition. All these labels. I mean, who cares? But now it’s fashion.” Hopkins also revealed that he suspects he inherited his late father Richard Hopkins’ mental health problems. “Oh yes, it crossed my mind that there was something not right with me,” he admitted. Hopkins shared with the Sunday Times that Laurence Olivier, who helped launch his career, once told him to see a psychiatrist, but he didn’t go. 7 Anthony Hopkins and his wife Stella Arroyave arrive for the premiere of ‘Transformers: The Last Knight’ at Civic Opera Building on June 20, 2017 in Chicago, Illinois. FilmMagic Hopkins, meanwhile, did see a therapist “briefly” at one point. “He kept saying, ‘Let’s go back ’ And I’d just go, ‘I don’t want to do this.’ So boring,’” Hopkins reflected, noting that he quit the session after learning his therapist had been married three times. Few entries into the horror genre have been as seminal as 1991’s The Silence of the Lambs , which is widely credited with inspiring a surge in horror thrillers featuring dangerous serial killers. The movie famously starred Jodie Foster as FBI trainee Clarice Starling and Anthony Hopkins as Hannibal Lecter , the cannibalistic and unnervingly insightful killer who assists Starling in the hunt for a serial murderer known as Buffalo Bill. One of the longest-standing rumors surrounding the movies is that the two actors barely spoke at all, due to Foster being deeply unsettled by Hopkins. Videos by ComicBook.com Jodie Foster has previously stated in interviews that she was too scared of Hopkins to speak to him after their first read-through of the script, and after hearing him become the horror movie icon Hannibal Lecter, she deliberately avoided him. Foster’s comments suggested that the pair barely spoke at all, but Anthony Hopkins recently revealed on Armchair Expert with Dax Shepard that this wasn’t at all the case. According to Hopkins, he and Foster were quite friendly on set while making The Silence of the Lambs , and any reports of tension had been deliberately played up for publicity. However, considering Foster has stated on multiple occasions how scared she was of Hopkins while making the movie, the theory about their relationship has only grown more complex after Hopkins’ latest comments. Read Next 5 Amazing Movie & TV Adaptations of Horror Novels (And Where to Stream Them) What Anthony Hopkins’ Recent Interview Tells Us About The Making Of The Silence Of The Lambs The fact that the two biggest stars of one of the most iconic horror thrillers in cinema have conflicting accounts of their relationship on set might seem to make the theories surrounding them more complex, but the truth is likely less interesting than it seems. Foster has stated on multiple occasions that she was terrified of Hopkins on set, and there’s very little evidence that actually disputes her account. In fact, Hopkins’ own comments don’t contradict Foster at all, but rather dismiss any claims of ill feeling between the pair. Considering Anthony Hopkins delivered an Oscar-winning turn as one of the creepiest horror movie villains of all time in The Silence of the Lambs , it’s not hard to see how Foster would have been unsettled. However, this doesn’t mean that Hopkins’ own claims that the pair were friendly are untrue, either. The main discrepancy lies in Foster stating that she barely spoke to and actively avoided Hopkins, while the Hannibal Lecter actor claims they were friendly toward one another. While they seem to contradict each other, the likely truth isn’t too difficult to surmise. In all likelihood, one is playing up the tension while the other plays it down. Foster almost certainly was somewhat afraid of Hopkins during filming, as his intense performance must have unnerved her on some level. However, that isn’t to say that things were at all unfriendly, as they were both experienced actors undertaking the task of playing roles opposite one another. The truth almost certainly lies more with Hopkins’ claims of a friendly relationship between the two, but perhaps with the distance suggested by Foster’s own admission of her fear of her co-star. Hopkins writes in his memoir We Did OK, Kid: "(Foster and I) mostly kept away from each other. Then, on our last day of shooting, we had lunch. It was freezing cold in Pittsburgh. Jodie put down her sandwich and said she had to confess something: she'd been scared of me." The legendary Welsh actor admitted he was also scared of Foster as the pair made light of their isolation. "We had a big hug, and we both admitted to feeling a strange sense of distance during the shoot, due no doubt to the power of that script, which had us playing a cat-and-mouse game," he said. "Since then, we've always greeted each other with great warmth." Foster - who won the Best Actress Oscar for her role - revealed she was frightened of Hopkins during the making of the film and believes her fear stemmed from techniques employed by director Jonathan Demme. "The movie didn't scare me, but Anthony Hopkins scared me," the 62-year-old actress said. "You'll notice, if you look at the movie again... instead of the person looking at the person off-screen, that the actors are actually looking down the lens. And that means I am there, but way behind the camera, and I'm just a voice; he can't see me. And the same is true on my side. "So when I'm doing scenes with Dr Lecter, I just hear this disembodied, scary voice, but I don't actually see his face. I have to look into the camera and pretend that he's in the camera." Hopkins said he "instinctively" knew how to play Lecter due to his inner "devil". "I knew the character instantly. I instinctively sensed how to play Hannibal. I have the devil in me. We all have the devil in us. I know what scares people." Foster, who recently starred in Nyad (2023), expressed excitement about her upcoming visit to Morocco, calling it "an honour to discover the beautiful city of Marrakech and to celebrate film at the same time." She added that she looks forward to introducing her new French film, Vie Privee (A Private Life), directed by Rebecca Zlotowski, at the festival. Mexican filmmaker Guillermo del Toro, a three-time Oscar winner for The Shape of Water and Guillermo del Toro's Pinocchio , will also be feted. Known for his imaginative visual storytelling in films like Pan's Labyrinth, Nightmare Alley and Crimson Peak, del Toro said he was "thrilled to return" to Marrakech and looked forward to presenting his upcoming Netflix project Frankenstein to festival audiences, according to The Hollywood Reporter . Moroccan actress Raouya—the stage name of Fatima Hernadi—has achieved great acclaim in film, television, and theatre, with performances in Thirst, Rock the Casbah and Cry No More . Expressing gratitude for being honoured in her homeland, Raouya said she shares a "deep friendship and loyalty" with the festival and its audience. Egyptian screen legend Hussein Fahmi, whose career spans more than five decades and includes over 100 films, will also be recognised. Among his most notable roles are in Watch Out for ZouZou , The Guilty and Alexandria: Again and Forever . Fahmi said being honoured in Marrakech holds special meaning as one of his earliest films, My Blood, My Tears, My Smile , was shot in the city. The Marrakech International Film Festival, established in 2001 under the patronage of King Mohammed VI, continues to be a major platform celebrating cinematic excellence and cultural exchange between global filmmakers. text: When Jodie Foster revealed she avoided Anthony Hopkins like plague on 'The Silence of the Lambs' sets ​ ​ ​ Login ​ Go Home Sports Movies Entertainment Photos National International Videos Business Kerala Health Home News When Jodie Foster revealed she avoided Anthony Hopkins like plague on 'The Silence of the Lambs' sets ​ By IANS | Published on ​ Mon, Nov 17 2025 22:10 IST | ​ 6 Views Los Angeles, Nov 17 : Hollywood actress Jodie Foster once revealed that she didn't speak with the acting legend Sir Anthony Hopkins during the filming of their cult film 'The Silence of the Lambs'. An old video from 'The Graham Norton Show' has resurfaced on the Internet, and it shows the actress recollecting her time on the sets of 'The Silence of the Lambs'. She said, "No, never spoke to him. He was scary. The first day we had a reading, we had like a little read-through. I got there early, and then I went to the bathroom, and I came back, everybody was sitting down. We did the read-through of the film. And by the end of it, I never wanted to talk to him again. And so then we did the whole movie. He was always behind the glass partitions. Because the scenes were so long, they'd kind of lock him in at the beginning of the day, and he'd go there, and then the next day, he'd be on the other side, and I'd be on this side. And we got to the end of the movie, and it really had never had a conversation". She further mentioned, "I avoided him. I really avoided him. And then I was eating a tuna fish sandwich. It was the last day of the shoot, and he came up to me, and I guess he sidled up to me, and I said, I don't know, I sort of had a tear in my eye. I was like, I was really scared of you. And he said, I was scared of you". 'The Silence of the Lambs', directed by Jonathan Demme, is a psychological thriller adapted from Thomas Harris's novel. It follows FBI trainee Clarice Starling (played by Jodie Foster), who seeks the help of imprisoned cannibalistic psychiatrist Dr. Hannibal Lecter to catch serial killer Buffalo Bill. The film is renowned for its tense storytelling, chilling performances, especially Anthony Hopkins's iconic portrayal of Lecter, and its exploration of manipulation, trauma, and power dynamics. It became one of the few films to win the Big Five' Academy Awards, Best Picture, Director, Actor, Actress, and Screenplay. The movie remains a landmark in suspense cinema and crime–psychological storytelling. An old video from 'The Graham Norton Show' has resurfaced on the Internet, and it shows the actress recollecting her time on the sets of 'The Silence of the Lambs'. She said, "No, never spoke to him. The first day we had a reading, we had like a little read-through. I got there early, and then I went to the bathroom, and I came back, everybody was sitting down. We did the read-through of the film. And by the end of it, I never wanted to talk to him again. And so then we did the whole movie. He was always behind the glass partitions. Because the scenes were so long, they'd kind of lock him in at the beginning of the day, and he'd go there, and then the next day, he'd be on the other side, and I'd be on this side. And we got to the end of the movie, and it really had never had a conversation". She further mentioned, "I avoided him. And then I was eating a tuna fish sandwich. It was the last day of the shoot, and he came up to me, and I guess he sidled up to me, and I said, I don't know, I sort of had a tear in my eye. I was like, I was really scared of you. And he said, I was scared of you". 'The Silence of the Lambs', directed by Jonathan Demme, is a psychological thriller adapted from Thomas Harris's novel. It follows FBI trainee Clarice Starling (played by Jodie Foster), who seeks the help of imprisoned cannibalistic psychiatrist Dr. Hannibal Lecter to catch serial killer Buffalo Bill. The film is renowned for its tense storytelling, chilling performances, especially Anthony Hopkins's iconic portrayal of Lecter, and its exploration of manipulation, trauma, and power dynamics. It became one of the few films to win the Big Five' Academy Awards, Best Picture, Director, Actor, Actress, and Screenplay. The movie remains a landmark in suspense cinema and crime–psychological storytelling. text: Guillermo del Toro, Jodie Foster to be honoured at Marrakech Film Festival Add ANI As A Trusted Source For Reliable Information Thu, Nov 27, 2025 | Updated 15:09 IST Toggle navigation Toggle navigation National General News Politics Features Business Entertainment Bollywood Hollywood Music Out of box Sports Cricket Football Others Tennis Hockey World Asia US Europe Pacific Others Middle East Health Tech Mobile Internet Science Others Videos National World Entertainment Sports Business Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Guillermo del Toro (Photo: Reuters) Guillermo del Toro, Jodie Foster to be honoured at Marrakech Film Festival ANI | Updated: Nov 04, 2025 20:04 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Marrakech [Morocco], November 4 (ANI): Oscar winners Guillermo del Toro and Jodie Foster will be honoured alongside Moroccan actress Raouya and Egyptian veteran Hussein Fahmi at the 22nd Marrakech International Film Festival , celebrating their outstanding contributions to global cinema. The festival, running from November 28 to December 6, described the honorees as "artists who embody the vitality of cinema and its ability to bring people together, move them, and inspire them," according to The Hollywood Reporter. Jodie Foster , a two-time Academy Award-winning actress known for films such as The Accused and The Silence of the Lambs, will be celebrated for her prolific career spanning over five decades. Foster, who recently starred in Nyad (2023), expressed excitement about her upcoming visit to Morocco, calling it "an honour to discover the beautiful city of Marrakech and to celebrate film at the same time." She added that she looks forward to introducing her new French film, "Vie Privee" (A Private Life), directed by Rebecca Zlotowski, at the festival. Mexican filmmaker Guillermo del Toro , a three-time Oscar winner for The Shape of Water and Guillermo del Toro 's Pinocchio, will also be feted. Known for his imaginative visual storytelling in films like Pan's Labyrinth, Nightmare Alley, and Crimson Peak, del Toro said he was "thrilled to return" to Marrakech and looked forward to presenting his upcoming Netflix project Frankenstein to festival audiences, according to The Hollywood Reporter. The festival will also celebrate two major Arab cinema personalities. Moroccan actress Raouya -- the stage name of Fatima Hernadi -- has achieved great acclaim in film, television, and theatre, with performances in Thirst, Rock the Casbah, and Cry No More. Expressing gratitude for being honoured in her homeland, Raouya said she shares a "deep friendship and loyalty" with the festival and its audience. Egyptian screen legend Hussein Fahmi , whose career spans more than five decades and includes over 100 films, will also be recognised. Among his most notable roles are in Watch Out for ZouZou, The Guilty, and Alexandria: Again and Forever. Fahmi said being honoured in Marrakech holds special meaning as one of his earliest films, My Blood, My Tears, My Smile, was shot in the city. The Marrakech International Film Festival , established in 2001 under the patronage of King Mohammed VI, continues to be a major platform celebrating cinematic excellence and cultural exchange between global filmmakers, according to The Hollywood Reporter. text: Marrakech Film Festival Honors Jodie Foster, Hussein Fahmi Among Other Cinema Icons Marrakech Film Festival Honors Jodie Foster, Hussein Fahmi Among Other Cinema Icons ADVERTISEMENT Prayer Times Morocco Lifestyle Western Sahara Login Register Home Culture Politics Society Economy Opinion Education Sustainability Tech Sport Genz 212 No Result View All Result Home Culture Politics Society Economy Opinion Education Sustainability Tech Sport Genz 212 No Result View All Result Home > Cinema > Marrakech Film Festival Honors Jodie Foster, Hussein Fahmi Among Other Cinema Icons Marrakech Film Festival Honors Jodie Foster, Hussein Fahmi Among Other Cinema Icons The festival will honor their exceptional contributions to world cinema, each representing a different region and embodying the diversity the festival celebrates. by Sara Zouiten Nov, 04, 2025 0 0 A A A A Reset The festival has celebrated artists who embody the power of cinema to bring people together, move audiences, and inspire creativity, Follow the latest news from Morocco World News Join on WhatsApp Join on Telegram Raba – The Marrakech International Film Festival will pay tribute to four major film figures during its 22nd edition, including American actress and director Jodie Foster, Mexican filmmaker Guillermo del Toro, Moroccan actress Raouya, and Egyptian actor Hussein Fahmi. For over two decades, the festival has celebrated artists who embody the power of cinema to bring people together, move audiences, and inspire creativity, organizers said in a press release. This year’s honorees represent the richness and diversity of world cinema, from Hollywood to North Africa and the Arab world. Jodie Foster began acting as a child and has built a remarkable career spanning more than 50 years. She has won two Academy Awards for her performances in “The Accused” as well as “The Silence of the Lambs”. Foster is also an acclaimed director, known for her thoughtful and powerful storytelling. “What an honor to discover your beautiful city of Marrakech and to celebrate film at the same time,” Foster said. “I can’t wait to experience the historic sites, gardens, and markets, to walk alongside new friends, colleagues, and movie lovers.” Meanwhile, Mexican director Guillermo del Toro is famous for creating poetic worlds where monsters and humans share the screen with equal beauty and sadness, says the statement. He is the winner of three Oscars, including for “The Shape of Water” and “Pinocchio”. “Since my previous visit, both the festival and the city have always been so welcoming to me. I’m especially honored to receive a tribute, and to show the audience my most personal work, Frankenstein,” del Toro said. Known by her fame name Raouya, Fatima Harandi is one of Morocco’s most beloved actresses. From theater to film, she has worked with leading Moroccan directors such as Narjiss Nejjar, Nour-Eddine Lakhmari, and Laïla Marrakchi. Her performances, including in “Les Yeux Secs” and “A Mile in My Shoes”, have earned her awards and national recognition. “What an immense honor it is to receive this invitation to the Marrakech International Film Festival. What joy and emotion to be celebrated in my own country, in the ochre city, at one of its largest film events,” Raouya stated. With a career spanning more than five decades, Hussein Fahmi is one of Egypt’s most respected actors. He has appeared in over 100 films and series and served as president of the Cairo International Film Festival. Fahmi is also known for his work promoting culture and dialogue across the Arab world. “The city of Marrakech has a special place in my heart as one of my earliest films, “Damy wa dmoy wa ebtsamty” (My Blood, My Tears, My Smile) was shot there. Coming back to this joyful city to be honored is a very precious moment,” Fahmi said. Foster is also an acclaimed director, known for her thoughtful and powerful storytelling. “What an honor to discover your beautiful city of Marrakech and to celebrate film at the same time,” Foster said. “I can’t wait to experience the historic sites, gardens, and markets, to walk alongside new friends, colleagues, and movie lovers. ” Meanwhile, Mexican director Guillermo del Toro is famous for creating poetic worlds where monsters and humans share the screen with equal beauty and sadness, says the statement. He is the winner of three Oscars, including for “The Shape of Water” and “Pinocchio”. “Since my previous visit, both the festival and the city have always been so welcoming to me. I’m especially honored to receive a tribute, and to show the audience my most personal work, Frankenstein,” del Toro said. Known by her fame name Raouya, Fatima Harandi is one of Morocco’s most beloved actresses. From theater to film, she has worked with leading Moroccan directors such as Narjiss Nejjar, Nour-Eddine Lakhmari, and Laïla Marrakchi. Her performances, including in “Les Yeux Secs” and “A Mile in My Shoes”, have earned her awards and national recognition. “What an immense honor it is to receive this invitation to the Marrakech International Film Festival. What joy and emotion to be celebrated in my own country, in the ochre city, at one of its largest film events,” Raouya stated. With a career spanning more than five decades, Hussein Fahmi is one of Egypt’s most respected actors. He has appeared in over 100 films and series and served as president of the Cairo International Film Festival. Fahmi is also known for his work promoting culture and dialogue across the Arab world. “The city of Marrakech has a special place in my heart as one of my earliest films, “Damy wa dmoy wa ebtsamty” (My Blood, My Tears, My Smile) was shot there. Coming back to this joyful city to be honored is a very precious moment,” Fahmi said. Image via Warner Bros. By Sam Barsanti Published 6 days ago Sam Barsanti has written about pop-culture for 10 years, and his work has appeared at The A.V. Club, Primetimer, IGN, and Collider. He has also contributed to the popular daily Hustle newsletter, which covers tech and startup news. He'll happily talk to anyone about comic book movies (he thinks the MCU peaked with Captain America: The Winter Soldier ) and giant robots (he thinks some of the Transformers movies are good), and he canonically exists in The CW's "Arrowverse" series of superhero shows. Sam is also a published poet and horror writer, and his fiction work has appeared on The No Sleep Podcast. Sign in to your Collider account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Memorable quotes in sci-fi movies tend to be things that are cool or interesting because of the context they’re spoken in. If you don’t know anything about Star Wars or The Terminator , “I am your father” and “I’ll be back” don't immediately seem noteworthy. Conversely, there are quotes that hit on something thematically important and grow beyond their origin, like “Life finds a way” from Jurassic Park or the “tears in rain” monologue from Blade Runner . One of the best quotes in sci-fi movie history, and maybe one of the best quotes in movie history period, is like that, and it comes from Robert Zemeckis ’ 1997 sci-fi drama Contact : “They should have sent a poet.” Contact is based on the novel of the same name by Carl Sagan , so he’s often credited for the quote (though Jodie Foster says it in the movie), and it’s about a scientist using radio signals to try and detect signs of intelligent alien life. Despite being a headier and more thoughtful sci-fi film than, say, Men In Black (which came out in theaters a week earlier), Contact played almost like a blockbuster and ultimately made $170 million on a $90 million budget . Sort of like a proto- Interstellar (it even has Matthew McConaughey ), reactions to Contact tend to land somewhere between “too sci-fi” and “not sci-fi enough,” but like a lot of Zemeckis’ more out-there projects , there’s magic to be found if you give yourself up to what he’s trying to do — which brings us to the quote. “They Should Have Sent a Poet” A shot of Jodie Foster inside a spaceship looking at the camera in Contact. Image via Warner Bros. Foster’s character, Dr. Eleanor Arroway, believes in her goal of detecting extraterrestrial life more than anyone else, despite political and financial pressure to do something more practical, but her faith is rewarded when she detects a signal coming from the direction of another star system . Aspects of the signal draw the attention of various governments around the world, and it ends up including the schematics for some sort of transportation pod that can ostensibly send one person somewhere. The original pilot is killed and Arroway is chosen to go in his place, so she is equipped with a bunch of recording devices and goes into the pod. It’s hard to explain what happens after that, but, luckily, Dr. Arroway sums it up nicely: “Some… celestial event. No. No words to describe it. Poetry. They should have sent a poet. ” The camera slowly zooms in, not on what Foster is seeing but on her face, selling the idea that she is witnessing something so transcendentally beautiful that nothing — not even Zemeckis’ love for groundbreaking special effects — can truly capture it. In short, they should’ve sent someone who knows how to use words to convey beauty, like a poet. Thus, Contact provided us with a perfect quote for when you see a thing you can’t describe, and one that is itself, ironically, pretty poetic. That means it can be used as an expression of beauty or majesty or something awe-inspiring, but it also makes for a pretty good joke (like when Danny DeVito ’s Frank Reynolds said it on an episode of I t’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia ). Imagine hanging out with your buds and somebody orders a really big, tasty-looking pizza. You drop “they should have sent a poet,” and it’ll kill . Thus, Contact provided us with a perfect quote for when you see a thing you can’t describe, and one that is itself, ironically, pretty poetic. The truth is, hair has no age limit. For women over 60, a shorter cut is a brilliant chance to experiment with different styles and textures, from the most striking pixie cuts to the more traditional bobs. What’s more, short hair can make you look younger , is often far easier to manage and allows you to perfectly highlight your best features. Whether you're after a sophisticated look for a special event or a practical everyday style, below I've detailed a variety of options to enhance your natural beauty and boost your confidence. Every woman is unique and deserves a hairstyle that truly reflects her personality and style. Unlike its all-round shorter counterpart, this style keeps extra length on top. This cut is great for those who want a modern low-maintenance look without sacrificing elegance, as shown by Kris Jenner, 70. The curly bob is designed specifically to help you embrace your hair's texture, enhancing it's beauty with a fresh, modern feel. It's easy to look after and style, giving your look fantastic volume and texture. 3 / 9 © Getty Images Sharon Stone The Mixie Cut This cut is an edgy marriage of the classic pixie and the contemporary mullet . Combining the short length of the pixie with the contrasting longer sections often found in a mullet, it offers a relaxed yet flattering style. Experts define this cut by a slightly longer nape (the back of the neck), giving it a rebellious yet sophisticated air that looks great on Sharon Stone, 67. 4 / 9 © Getty Images Naomi Campbell The French Bob This chic Anna Wintour-esque style is characterised by a blunt length that typically sits around the jawline or slightly above, creating a defined and flattering frame for the face. The straight, neat bangs frame the eyes and adds a touch of sophistication - a timeless, versatile look, perfect for those seeking a chic, polished vibe. 5 / 9 © Getty Images for BFI Cate Blanchett The Classic Bob The classic bob is an ageless and universally flattering choice because of it's timelessness - it always looks current. Its length, which usually reaches the jawline or a little lower, creates a defined line that softens the features. Simple to style and care for, it's a practical choice for everyday life. 6 / 9 © Getty Images for Sports Illustra Roshumba Williams The Micro Pixie For those women who defy the stereotypes of age and aren't afraid of a dramatic change, the micro pixie is the perfect choice. This ultra-short cut s a bold statement that simply exudes confidence. Designed for those seeking a modern, edgy look, this one will make you stand out from the crowd at any age. 7 / 9 © FilmMagic, Jodie Foster The Layered Cut If your hair is fine and lacks volume , a short, above-the-shoulder layered cut is just what you need. This style not only looks youthful - just check out Jodie Foster, 63 - but also adds a sense of fullness and movement to your hair . Strategically cut layers create the illusion of greater volume, while the shorter length prevents the hair from falling flat or looking heavy. 8 / 9 © Getty Images for amfAR Retro waves Evoking Old Hollywood, this short, side-swept cut with waves is the epitome of glamour. The combination of the shorter length and soft waves creates a sophisticated look that still looks right at home in the 21st century. Styling the hair swept to one side accentuates the face, particularly the cheekbones. And the near shoulder length of this style makes it optimal if you want versatility for day-to-day looks and special occasions, too. 9 / 9 © Getty Images Dame Helen Mirren The Asymmetrical Bob How chic does Dame Helen look with her grey hair ? The 80-year-old star's bob gets a contemporary edge thanks to the sleek, straight finish. This look can be easily tailored to any face shape by simply adjusting the parting and the length, but it particularly suits those with softer, less defined features. Photo: AP PHOTO Anthony Hopkins and Jodie Foster have revealed they stayed away from each other during the making of The Silence of the Lambs. Create a free account to read this article Login or signup to continue reading Continue with Email Continue with Google Continue with Apple The 87-year-old star won the Academy Award for Best Actor for his portrayal of serial killer Dr Hannibal Lecter in the 1991 film and said Foster, who played FBI trainee Clarice Starling, kept her distance because she was "scared" of him. Hopkins writes in his memoir We Did OK, Kid: "(Foster and I) mostly kept away from each other. Then, on our last day of shooting, we had lunch. It was freezing cold in Pittsburgh. Jodie put down her sandwich and said she had to confess something: she'd been scared of me." The legendary Welsh actor admitted he was also scared of Foster as the pair made light of their isolation. "We had a big hug, and we both admitted to feeling a strange sense of distance during the shoot, due no doubt to the power of that script, which had us playing a cat-and-mouse game," he said. "Since then, we've always greeted each other with great warmth." Foster - who won the Best Actress Oscar for her role - revealed she was frightened of Hopkins during the making of the film and believes her fear stemmed from techniques employed by director Jonathan Demme. "The movie didn't scare me, but Anthony Hopkins scared me," the 62-year-old actress said. "You'll notice, if you look at the movie again... instead of the person looking at the person off-screen, that the actors are actually looking down the lens. And that means I am there, but way behind the camera, and I'm just a voice; he can't see me. And the same is true on my side. "So when I'm doing scenes with Dr Lecter, I just hear this disembodied, scary voice, but I don't actually see his face. I have to look into the camera and pretend that he's in the camera." Hopkins said he "instinctively" knew how to play Lecter due to his inner "devil". "I knew the character instantly. I instinctively sensed how to play Hannibal. I have the devil in me. We all have the devil in us. I know what scares people." And that means I am there, but way behind the camera, and I'm just a voice; he can't see me. And the same is true on my side. "So when I'm doing scenes with Dr Lecter, I just hear this disembodied, scary voice, but I don't actually see his face. I have to look into the camera and pretend that he's in the camera." Hopkins said he "instinctively" knew how to play Lecter due to his inner "devil". "I knew the character instantly. I instinctively sensed how to play Hannibal. I have the devil in me. We all have the devil in us. I know what scares people." The Moroccan fest, which runs from Nov. 28 to Dec. 6, will also host talks with “The Matrix” actor Laurence Fishburne; “Blonde” director Andrew Dominik; “It Was Just an Accident” helmer and this year’s Palme d’Or winner director Jafar Panahi; Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences CEO Bill Kramer; “The Secret Agent” director Kleber Mendonça Filho; Bollywood director Karan Johan; Lebanese director and actor Nadine Labaki; “A Prophet” actor Tahar Rahim; and Egyptian actor Yousra. By Maansi V 22 November 2025 Dystopian movies can be unsettling, not just because they show ruined worlds or strict governments, but because many of them feel like they could actually happen. These movies take real issues – technology , climate change, politics , surveillance, social media pressure – and push them just a little further to show what might come next. They are gripping, thought-provoking, and sometimes uncomfortably familiar. If you’ve ever watched a movie and thought, ‘This is way too close to real life,’ this list is for you. 7 dystopian movies that feel uncomfortably real today; on JioHotstar, YouTube & more ​1. Children of Men – Amazon Prime Video Set in 2027, the world is in crisis because humans have become infertile, and no child has been born for 18 years. Society is crumbling, governments are cracking down, refugees are being hunted, and everyday life feels unstable. In the middle of this bleak world, a cynical former activist is asked to protect a young woman who holds an extraordinary secret. The movie’s dystopia isn’t built on flashy sci-fi ideas; it’s grounded in things we already see today, like immigration debates, police militarisation, social fear, propaganda, and the way people adapt to constant crises. Its gritty style makes it feel less like fiction and more like a glimpse into a possible future. ​2. V For Vendetta – YouTube Set in a future Britain ruled by a harsh authoritarian government, the story follows a masked vigilante known only as V (played by Hugo Weaving), who tries to spark a revolution against the regime. When he crosses paths with a young woman named Evey (Natalie Portman), she becomes an unexpected part of his mission. What makes the movies feel so real is the backdrop of V’s mission – surveillance everywhere, controlled media, fear-driven politics, and the slow loss of freedom. Its themes of resistance and the power of ordinary citizens feel especially relevant today. ​3. 1984 – Amazon Prime Video Based on George Orwell’s classic novel , the plot unfolds in a grim future where a totalitarian government monitors every move its citizens make. Individual freedom is squashed, independent thinking is forbidden, and history is constantly rewritten to suit the ruling Party’s needs. In this suffocating world, one man, Winston Smith (John Hurt), begins to question everything he has been taught to obey when he falls in love with Julia (Suzanna Hamilton). Even decades later, 1984 still mirrors many modern anxieties (mass surveillance, manipulated information, slow erosion of truth), making it one of the most unsettlingly believable dystopias ever made. ​4. The Purge – Amazon Prime Video Set in a near-future America, the government declares one night every year when all crime, including violent crime, is completely legal for 12 hours. The story follows the Sandin family trying to stay safe inside their fortified home, but the night takes a dangerous turn when moral chaos ensues. The movie uses an extreme setup to explore very real issues: rising inequality, unchecked violence, political manipulation, and how fear can be turned into policy. Its world may be exaggerated, but the social tensions at its core feel unsettlingly familiar. ​5. Fahrenheit 451 – JioHotstar A tightly controlled future America has erased books from society, turning firemen into enforcers who hunt down and burn the last traces of written knowledge. One of these firemen, Guy Montag ( Michael B. Jordan ) , praised as a hero, begins to question his role after he meets Clarisse (Sofia Boutella), an informant. The encounter opens his eyes to what the government is hiding and what people are losing. Its focus on digital dependence, algorithmic control, and the policing of information makes the story feel uncomfortably close to today’s world. The tech-driven twist offers a modern take on Ray Bradbury’s classic novel. ​6. Elysium – YouTube In the year 2154, the rich live comfortably on a luxurious space station called Elysium, while everyone else struggles to survive on an overcrowded, polluted Earth. Max Da Costa (Matt Damon), a factory worker, meets with a deadly accident and only has days to live. Desperate to reach Elysium’s advanced medical technology, he agrees to a risky mission. Meanwhile, Secretary Delacourt (Jodie Foster) will do whatever it takes to protect the perfect world she controls, and a ruthless agent named Kruger (Sharlto Copley) is sent to stop Max at any cost. While the movie exaggerates the gap between rich and poor, the ideas are very close to modern reality – unequal access to healthcare, overcrowded cities, strict border control, and powerful people living far away from the problems everyone else faces. It's a picture of a future divided by wealth, privilege, and technology. ​7. Soylent Green – Amazon Prime Video In a crowded and polluted New York of the future, Detective Thorn (Charlton Heston) is asked to investigate the death of William Simonson, a wealthy and influential man. As Thorn digs deeper, with help from his elderly roommate Sol Roth (Edward G. Robinson), he starts to realise that the city’s food crisis and the popular product Soylent Green may be hiding a dark secret. The more he uncovers, the more dangerous the truth becomes. The film tackles issues like climate crisis, overpopulation, corporate power, and resource scarcity; problems the world is already worrying about. Its imagined future doesn’t feel far-off; it feels like a warning sign. By Marcus James Dixon Plus icon Marcus James Dixon More stories by Marcus ‘Stranger Things 5’ reviews: It’s ‘still a hell of a ride,’ say critics, as the first 4 episodes hit Netflix 0 Comments Read more Matt and Ross Duffer tease Max’s fate in ‘Stranger Things 5’: ‘It’ll surprise people how she comes into the show’ 0 Comments Read more Nicole Kidman and Jamie Lee Curtis are sisters in ‘Scarpetta’: Everything to know about Prime Video’s TV adaptation 0 Comments Read more November 18, 2025 11:30 am The Chronology of Water The Forge/Courtesy Everett Collection Share Share on Facebook Post google Google Preferred Pin it Show more sharing options Share to Flipboard Post to Tumblr Submit to Reddit Share on LinkedIn Share on WhatsApp Email Print This Page 1 Kristen Stewart is returning to movie theaters, but this time she's behind the camera. The Twilight megastar and Spencer Oscar nominee is the director, writer, and producer of The Chronology of Water , a biographical romantic drama that's adapted from the 2011 memoir by Lidia Yuknavitch . The film received raves at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival in May, where it was featured in the Un Certain Regard section. Read on for everything to know about The Chronology of Water before it hits theaters. Imogen Poots , Kristen Stewart, Thora Birch Priscilla Grant/Everett Collection WHO'S IN THE CAST? Imogen Poots plays the lead role of Lidia Yuknavitch, the real-life subject of the story. Notable supporting actors include Thora Birch as Claudia, Susannah Flood as Dorothy, Tom Sturridge as Kevin, and Jim Belushi as Ken. Kristen Stewart does not appear on camera in the film. Related Stories ‘Stranger Things 5’ reviews: It’s ‘still a hell of a ride,’ say critics, as the first 4 episodes hit Netflix Matt and Ross Duffer tease Max’s fate in ‘Stranger Things 5’: ‘It’ll surprise people how she comes into the show’ WHAT'S THE PLOT? The Chronology of Water follows a young Lidia as she navigates childhood trauma and finds her voice through writing and swimming. The narrative culminates in her becoming a successful teacher, mother, and unique contemporary author. WATCH THE TRAILER On Nov. 18, the two-minute trailer was released by the Forge. "I thought about starting at the beginning," Poots says in voice-over, as we see various images including water mixed with blood. "But that's not how I remember it. It's all a series, fragments, repetitions, patterns, formations." The character of Lidia's childhood is briefly hinted at, as she experiences an abusive household. At the end of the video, Poots stares at the camera and wonders aloud, "Memories are stories, so you better come up with one you can live with." WHO'S BEHIND THE SCENES? Stewart is the director and co-screenwriter, alongside Andy Mingo . Joining her as a producer are Michael Pruss , Rebecca Feuer , Charles Gillibert , Yulia Zayceva , Max Pavlov , Svetlana Punte , Maggie McLean , and Dylan Meyer . Artisans include cinematographer Corey C. Waters , editor Olivia Neergaard-Holm , composer Paris Hurley , production designer Jen Dunlap , and costume designer Liene Dobraja . WHAT IS THE RELEASE DATE? Following its May premiere in Cannes, The Chronology of Water is scheduled for a limited theatrical release in the United States beginning on Dec. 5. It will be released nationwide on Jan. 9. Kristen Stewart at the 2025 Governors Awards KRISTEN STEWART'S AWARDS HISTORY The film is eligible at the 2026 Oscars and other upcoming awards. Stewart is no stranger to the Oscars , receiving a Best Actress nomination for Spencer (2021) — she lost to Jessica Chastain for The Eyes of Tammy Faye . Stewart won the Rising Star Award at the 2010 BAFTAs and the Tribute Award at the 2021 Gothams. She also received bids for Spencer at the Golden Globes and Critics Choice Awards. Dark Horizons All Stories Movie News TV News Game News Trailers Reviews Features Release Dates 2025 Movie Release Dates 4K & Blu-ray Release Dates PC Game Release Dates PS5 Release Dates Xbox Series X Release Dates Nintendo Switch Release Dates Movie News Trailers Trailer: Kristen Stewart’s “Chronology of Water” By Garth Franklin - Tuesday, November 18th 2025 12:40 pm The Forge The first trailer has been released for the biographical romantic drama “The Chronology of Water,” based on the 2011 autobiographical novel by Lidia Yuknavitch. Acclaimed actress Kristen Stewart makes her feature film directorial debut on the project, which stars Imogen Poots as a professional swimmer and Olympic hopeful who is on a journey of self-exploration. The film traces Lidia’s life from her earliest memories in the Pacific Northwest, as a promising swimmer, through fractured relationships, a raging father, an alcoholic and suicidal mother, near-motherhood, addiction, promiscuous sex, and encounters with artistic heroes. Told as a fluid memory wash, the story transforms trauma into art, embodying Yuknavitch’s defiant voice. It is not only a chronicle of a woman becoming a writer, but a visceral journey through the wreckage and resilience of a life lived against the grain. The film also stars Thora Birch as Claudia, Susannah Flood as Dorothy, Tom Sturridge as Kevin, and Jim Belushi as Ken Kesey. “The Chronology of Water” premiered at the Cannes Film Festival and sits at a 94% on Rotten Tomatoes. It hits select cinemas on December 5th and goes wide on January 9th.
