text: Issa Rae admits she doesn't feel successful Skip to content News Entertainment Culture Business Health IQ Beauty Videos Experiences News Entertainment Culture Business Health IQ Beauty Videos Experiences Close Open Search Search Home » TV Issa Rae admits she doesn’t feel successful The versatitle actress, writer, producer and author is in a state of frustration By Terry Shropshire Nov 15, 2025 8:55 am Issa Rae (Photo credit: Shutterstock.com / DFree) By any traditional metric, multi-hyphenate entertainer and storyteller Issa Rae is a success story. A writer, producer, actress, and entrepreneur with a cultural footprint most creatives only dream of, she built an empire from a YouTube series and turned it into “Insecure” — a five-season HBO phenomenon that reshaped the entertainment landscape for Black storytelling on television. She’s launched businesses, produced films and series across genres, and just released a new book. Despite the blizzard of activity, awards, and accolades, Issa Rae says she doesn’t feel successful right now. Issa Rae feels stagnant On the debut episode of “Not My Best Moment with KevOnStage,” released Nov. 12, Rae sat down with host Kevin Fredericks and offered a surprising confession: despite the accolades, despite the empire, she feels “stagnant.” “I know that I appear successful to other people, but right now, no,” s he said in a clip from the conversation. “I feel really stagnant.” For Rae, success isn’t abstract or philosophical — it’s visceral. It’s literal. It’s whether or not she has a show on air. When Issa Rae does feel successful “I only really feel a sense of success when my sh— is on the air,” she explained. It’s a startling admission from someone whose creative output seems constant. Since Insecure ended, Rae has acted in hit films, shepherded new voices through her production company, published books, and cultivated an ecosystem of artistic ventures. But for her, none of it replaces the singular thrill of getting a TV project out into the world. “Like, I can have the 18 businesses,” she told Fredericks. “And those are great passion projects, but what I do—and what I get excited about—isn’t happening right now.” When Issa Rae feels ‘like nothing’ Fredericks joked: so once a movie comes out or a series finale airs … does she go right back to feeling like she’s “nothing”? Rae laughed, but didn’t disagree. “Yeah. I haven’t put words to it but that’s exactly how it feels. ‘I am nothing again’ is crazy… it’s so real.” That tension — between external achievement and internal satisfaction — is something Rae explores in her latest book, I Should Be Smarter Now , a collection of essays tracing the highs, lows, and hard-won lessons of her career. She writes candidly about the impulsive decisions that have nearly cost her everything, and the fearlessness that has just as often propelled her forward. Issa Rae explains ‘the gift and the curse’ “My impulsivity… is both a gift and a curse,” she writes. “The gift is that I can be fearless in the pursuit of anything I want to achieve. If I want something, I’m going to be active and go after it.” But even with that drive, Rae admits she’s learning to sit with career quietness— and the discomfort that comes with it. She says she’s staying optimistic. She’s staying focused. She’s building. But successful? Not right now, she says. It’s a reminder that even the creatives who seem unstoppable, unshakeable, and unquestionably accomplished can look at their own journey and wonder: What’s next? She’s launched businesses, produced films and series across genres, and just released a new book. Despite the blizzard of activity, awards, and accolades, Issa Rae says she doesn’t feel successful right now. Issa Rae feels stagnant On the debut episode of “Not My Best Moment with KevOnStage,” released Nov. 12, Rae sat down with host Kevin Fredericks and offered a surprising confession: despite the accolades, despite the empire, she feels “stagnant. ” “I know that I appear successful to other people, but right now, no,” s he said in a clip from the conversation. ” For Rae, success isn’t abstract or philosophical — it’s visceral. It’s whether or not she has a show on air. When Issa Rae does feel successful “I only really feel a sense of success when my sh— is on the air,” she explained. It’s a startling admission from someone whose creative output seems constant. Since Insecure ended, Rae has acted in hit films, shepherded new voices through her production company, published books, and cultivated an ecosystem of artistic ventures. But for her, none of it replaces the singular thrill of getting a TV project out into the world. “Like, I can have the 18 businesses,” she told Fredericks. “And those are great passion projects, but what I do—and what I get excited about—isn’t happening right now. ” When Issa Rae feels ‘like nothing’ Fredericks joked: so once a movie comes out or a series finale airs … does she go right back to feeling like she’s “nothing”? Rae laughed, but didn’t disagree. I haven’t put words to it but that’s exactly how it feels. ‘I am nothing again’ is crazy… it’s so real. ” That tension — between external achievement and internal satisfaction — is something Rae explores in her latest book, I Should Be Smarter Now , a collection of essays tracing the highs, lows, and hard-won lessons of her career. She writes candidly about the impulsive decisions that have nearly cost her everything, and the fearlessness that has just as often propelled her forward. Issa Rae explains ‘the gift and the curse’ “My impulsivity… is both a gift and a curse,” she writes. “The gift is that I can be fearless in the pursuit of anything I want to achieve. If I want something, I’m going to be active and go after it. ” But even with that drive, Rae admits she’s learning to sit with career quietness— and the discomfort that comes with it. She says she’s staying optimistic. But successful? Not right now, she says. It’s a reminder that even the creatives who seem unstoppable, unshakeable, and unquestionably accomplished can look at their own journey and wonder: What’s next? I was supposed to be writing beats for her, but I ultimately just started writing the script.” She also revealed the she and Rae have been discussing plans for the movie over Zoom adding the characters in the film will be “thinly-veiled versions” of themselves while also adding “The characters’ names [are] Lena and Issa, I’m not even being that imaginative about it.” Waithe added, they “want to” play themselves in the film. “Issa’s going to be like, ‘Oh s***, well now we got to do it.” This Will Mark Lena Waithe’s First Film Since 2019’s Queen & Slim This latest news comes on the heels of Waite wrapping up her Showtime drama, The Chi , which will finally end after eight seasons, putting it in the same category as other Showtime series Dexter , Homeland and Weeds as the network’s second-longest running series. Whenever this film begins production, it will be the first project since the controversial 2019 film, Queen & Slim that starred Daniel Kaluuyah and Jodie Turner-Smith which sparked alot of dicussions about its plot revolving around a Black couple on the run after shooting a cop accidentally following a blind date. Despite the fallout, speaking with Deadline , Waithe said she is still making films telling the website in an interview “As for what the future holds, I still plan on telling stories, continuing to build community, and making space for us all to be seen.” For Rae, she is coming off 2023’s box office hit Barbie and the critically acclaimed American Fiction . Eater.com Facebook Twitter Instagram Youtube RSS Dining Reports Hot Supper Club Somerville Cooks for South Los Angeles Though elegance radiates from this View Park-Windsor Hills restaurant, service, jazz, and food comes without the fuss by Mona Holmes Oct 29, 2025, 5:30 PM UTC Facebook Link Brunch dishes at Somerville. Jakob Layman Mona Holmes is an editor at Eater Southern California/Southwest, a regular contributor at KCRW radio, and a 2022 James Beard Award nominee. Somerville can take your breath away. The sensational View Park-Windsor Hills restaurant debuted in November 2024 with a stunning mahogany wood Art Deco-style room, white oak flooring, custom banquettes, and a grand piano on a modest stage where live jazz is often played. Owners Yonnie Hagos, Ajay Relan, and collaborator Issa Rae (yes, the actor and producer) brought to life something that South LA has long been lacking: a fine dining restaurant that keeps its residents from traveling outside of the neighborhood while paying tribute to Black Los Angeles history. Chef Geter Atienza prepares crudos, braised lamb shank, a Black Angus burger, and wagyu strip loin, among other supper club-style dishes. Every element of the room is elegant, as is the crowd. What to order Order Parker house rolls with truffle butter for the table immediately upon sitting. They’ll land just as you’re ready to order everything else. Deeply rich braised short rib gets sauced Perigaux-style and served over truffle risotto with crimini mushrooms. Fill the table with the organic roasted chicken, baked macaroni and cheese, charred broccolini, and Peruvian scallop crudo to share. At brunch, the blue crab quiche with a glass of sparkling wine is all one needs. The formidable John Coltrane cocktail A Love Supreme mixes vodka, Midori, Cointreau, and lemon. The vibe Though Somerville has no official dress code, plan to dress up to participate in the owners’ honoring of the long-gone Hotel Somerville and the former adjacent Central Avenue jazz venues from the 1940s . Insider tip Reservations are a must: Somerville remains one of the hottest seats in town. If fully booked, ask for a bar seat, which has the best vantage point of the stage. Somerville dining room. Jakob Layman Somerville Location 4437 West Slauson Avenue, Los Angeles, California 90043 External Link Phone (323) 815-1505 Link https://www.somervilleslauson.com/ A sumptuous supper club just opened on Slauson Avenue from Yonnie Hagos and Ajay Relan, the duo behind the budding chain of Hilltop Coffee + Kitchen shops and Downtown’s Lost Rooftop Cocktail + Taco Bar . Their first Los Angeles restaurant, Somerville , offers full-service, compelling cocktails, a curated wine list, live music, and American food standards, including Parker house rolls, Black Angus burgers, fried chicken and caviar sliders, and more. text: The 2025 Black Beauty Roster Creator Summit Was Filled With Endless Gems - Essence | Essence Skip to content Essence GU Beautycon NaturallyCurly Afropunk Essence Studios Soko Mrkt Ese Funds Refinery29 2025 ESSENCE Festival Of Culture Celebrity Fashion Beauty Lifestyle Entrepreneurship News Shopping Video Events Subscribe Home • Awards & Events The 2025 Black Beauty Roster Creator Summit Was A Day Filled With Endless Gems For this year’s BBR Creator Summit, panelists got down into the details of what it takes to thrive as a beauty creator today. Courtesy of Black Beauty Roster By Cierra Black · Updated November 11, 2025 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready… The Black Beauty Roster Creator Summit kicked off for another year with an expanded program, new venue, and re-energized atmosphere. Along with an exciting roster of media personalities on the docket, the itinerary included back-to-back panels that pored over some of the most pressing topics facing beauty influencers in today’s landscape. This year’s lineup, powered by Brown Sugar Babe , boasted a plethora of beauty professionals and digital commentators, from brand founders such as Danessa Myricks and Hannah Diop to media personalities Kayla Nicole and JaNa Craig. Culminating in a fireside chat featuring entertainment and beauty mogul Issa Rae in conversation with media professional Nina Parker , the BBR Creator Summit dug into everything from balancing mental health, finances, self-advocacy, and creative integrity. The atmosphere was a true manifestation of beauty: fashion, hairstyles, vibrant colors, blush hues, and perfume scents—it was a beauty girl’s closet come to life. So much so that a quick bathroom break between panels found every single sink occupied by attendees brushing their hair, reapplying gloss, or adding some blush to their cheeks. It felt like a hub for beauty girls to play in their medium and be themselves. Held in the heart of Los Angeles’ Koreatown, the event saw a large ballroom filled with attendees soaking in the conversations of the day, while the second floor welcomed even more guests to an exhibition room housing a plethora of Black-owned beauty brands showcasing their products and executing live demonstrations. An impromptu booth visit by Danessa Myricks found her quickly surrounded by supporters eager to soak in what she had to offer. The charismatic Monica Veloz , known across digital platforms as “MonicaStyleMuse,” served as the most vibrant host, strutting across the stage to Bad Bunny and setting the energy right for the sequence of events. She kicked off opening remarks by introducing Maude Okrah Hunter, founder of Black Beauty Roster, who gave a warm welcome honing in on purpose, story, and community before handing the microphone to Maekaeda Gibbons, founder of Brown Sugar Babe, to speak additional affirmations over the guests looking back at them. Veloz wove humorous and heartfelt commentary into the room as she flowed through the introductions of nine panels, a morning mindfulness activity, and the culminating fireside chat with Issa Rae, engaging the audience with questions, takeaways, and a fabulous outfit change. A touching reminder she graced the audience with included the importance of talking to your circle to, “get your dreams realized.” Speaking life into yourself and sharing it with a community that can help connect you further down your path will do wonders, and is the very act that brought her the opportunity to host that day. Consistent with last year’s summit, the day commenced with a grounding meditation, led by yogi and mindfulness leader Alicia Easter . The theme for the meditation was “sparking joy in the midst of chaos,” and accepting wherever you may be in your journey—a relevant concept for an industry where constant information, comparison, overstimulation, and visibility is the norm. The first panel that followed saw Headspace Mindfulness Educator Dora Kamau moderate Karen Civil , Obio Jones , and Dexter Mayfield as they discussed striking the balance between pushing forward in public-facing careers while nurturing themselves through the trials of life. The experts emphasized carving out intentional time to be present in their bodies, taking the shame out of setting healthy boundaries, and making space for both grief and gratitude while navigating life’s losses with career success. On the theme of centering intentionality in content and work, four panels delved into the power and art of storytelling, embracing the multi-hyphenate era, grappling with the ethics of AI, and the beauty of collaboration. Digital creator DonYé Taylor moderated a discussion with Sahar Khorramnezhad , Cindy Nwachukwu , and Shantelle Dockett as they discussed how transformative sharing your own personal story can be, and finding the through line of your “why.” Love Island breakout star-turned-media-doll JaNa Craig spoke to the blessings curiosity can lead to as she discussed embracing a career that incorporates her ever-evolving interests (spoken like a true Sagittarius). Her co-panelist, Tanya Marie , shared, “don’t allow the world to put you in a box. Lean into who you are, your personality, your identity. That’s when magic happens.” Danessa Myricks was a consistent favorite of the day, as multiple panelists stopped mid-sentence to greet her with excitement and speak about how impactful her work and presence is to the beauty landscape. With her panel on collaboration, she spoke about the need to see alignment in all that you do: “You can lose your entire community by doing something that’s not authentic to who you are.” Inside of the highly-anticipated panel with media personality Kayla Nicole , she along with beauty and media favorites Julissa Bermudez , Marvella and MakeupShayla , enlightened beauty creators on how to expand your passions beyond the screen for a career that can last past trending moments. Nicole shared a genuine and emotional moment with the beauties in the room to discuss how difficult it can be to be on the receiving end of so much feedback, namely as a Black woman facing bigoted audiences. Through it all, she finds grace and optimism in the impact she sees when she champions mental health and vulnerability. An important yet uncomfortable topic for many marginalized people navigating business includes finances, advocacy, and investments. This can feel all the more true in the influencer economy where there are many factors at play, which is why BBR Summit made a pointed effort to facilitate several conversations focusing on building financial freedom, diversifying income, and taking an inside look at how brands such as Pinterest and Visa build with creators for lasting impact. Executives from such companies and those like WME and Tarte gave invaluable advice on how to best protect your financial health amidst the madness. To close out the day, journalist and host Nina Parker took the stage with Issa Rae for an insightful, inspiring, and timely conversation. The two reflected on Rae’s career from Awkward Black Girl and Insecure to the big screen and successful hospitality and beauty ventures. The way Rae sees all of these worlds coming together? “I love to tell stories. I love to eat. I love community.” And sometimes when it comes to building a world that makes sense, it is as simple as that. The two media mavens spoke about the makings of Rae’s career, and she offered much-needed encouragement and advice for all those looking to find their place and tell their own story. The Black Beauty Roster Creator Summit concluded for another year, leaving an array of Black beauty influencers with food for thought, budding connections, and reinvigorated mindsets to take on the consumer landscape that would not run without them. Lean into who you are, your personality, your identity. ” Danessa Myricks was a consistent favorite of the day, as multiple panelists stopped mid-sentence to greet her with excitement and speak about how impactful her work and presence is to the beauty landscape. With her panel on collaboration, she spoke about the need to see alignment in all that you do: “You can lose your entire community by doing something that’s not authentic to who you are. ” Inside of the highly-anticipated panel with media personality Kayla Nicole , she along with beauty and media favorites Julissa Bermudez , Marvella and MakeupShayla , enlightened beauty creators on how to expand your passions beyond the screen for a career that can last past trending moments. Nicole shared a genuine and emotional moment with the beauties in the room to discuss how difficult it can be to be on the receiving end of so much feedback, namely as a Black woman facing bigoted audiences. Through it all, she finds grace and optimism in the impact she sees when she champions mental health and vulnerability. An important yet uncomfortable topic for many marginalized people navigating business includes finances, advocacy, and investments. This can feel all the more true in the influencer economy where there are many factors at play, which is why BBR Summit made a pointed effort to facilitate several conversations focusing on building financial freedom, diversifying income, and taking an inside look at how brands such as Pinterest and Visa build with creators for lasting impact. Executives from such companies and those like WME and Tarte gave invaluable advice on how to best protect your financial health amidst the madness. To close out the day, journalist and host Nina Parker took the stage with Issa Rae for an insightful, inspiring, and timely conversation. The two reflected on Rae’s career from Awkward Black Girl and Insecure to the big screen and successful hospitality and beauty ventures. The way Rae sees all of these worlds coming together? “I love to tell stories. ” And sometimes when it comes to building a world that makes sense, it is as simple as that. The two media mavens spoke about the makings of Rae’s career, and she offered much-needed encouragement and advice for all those looking to find their place and tell their own story. The Black Beauty Roster Creator Summit concluded for another year, leaving an array of Black beauty influencers with food for thought, budding connections, and reinvigorated mindsets to take on the consumer landscape that would not run without them. By Kay Wicker Nov 14, 2025 Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share via Email Copy Link Link Copied Issa Rae attends the 2025 Met Gala Celebrating "Superfine: Tailoring Black Style" at Metropolitan Museum of Art on May 05, 2025 in New York City. (Photo by Savion Washington/Getty Images) Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share via Email Copy Link Link Copied Issa Rae , if you can believe it, deals with feeling less than successful, too. On the debut episode of the new podcast “ Not My Best Moment with KevOnStage ,” hosted by comedian and actor Kevin Fredericks released on Nov. 12, the “Churchy” star sat down with the “Insecure” creator, who revealed she struggles with feeling “stagnant.” “I know that I appear successful to other people, but right now, no, I feel really stagnant,” Rae admitted in a clip . The 40-year-old writer and producer added that the feeling is “literal” because she only really feels a sense of success “when my sh— is on the air.” Rae, who became a cultural force after launching HBO’s “Insecure,” which ran for five seasons and became a defining touchstone of Black millennial life, has since gone on to star in hit films, produce acclaimed projects across genres, release books, and build an expansive creative empire. But as she explained, TV is her true passion. When she’s not on our screens, she’s laser-focused on getting back there. “Like, I can have the 18 businesses,” she continued. “And those are, like, great passion projects, but like, what I do and what I get excited about isn’t happening right now.” Fredericks jokingly asked if once a movie is out or once a show finishes airing, she goes back to feeling like “nothing” again. “Yeah,” she said, laughing. “I haven’t put words to it but that’s exactly how it feels. I am nothing again is crazy … it’s so real.” The actress has long been open about the hurdles she’s had to overcome to even get one project made. This latest admission arrives on the heels of Rae’s latest release, “I Should Be Smarter Now ,” a collection of essays that spans her career and the lessons she’s learned thus far. In it, she writes about one mistake in particular that nearly cost her all of the money she’d earned up to that point, brought on by her “impulsivity.” “My impulsivity, the character trait I’ve benefited from and paid dearly for, is both a gift and a curse,” Rae wrote. “The gift is that I can be fearless in the pursuit of anything I want to achieve. Mike Coppola/Getty Images By Donnetta Monk · Updated November 21, 2025 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready… This holiday season, I am retiring my extra small knotless braids in exchange for creative low-tension styles. I knew it was time to reset when, this summer, I found a small bald spot, aka traction alopecia, at the crown of my head from back-to-back tight styles. With scalp serums, a consistent routine, and a break from trendy high-tension styles, my scalp is healing. The simple pleated braids we wore in elementary school with bobos have reinvented themselves. Low-tension styles are no longer just a few neat plaits. They have evolved thanks to curly hair stylists and influencers. I am not alone. My feeds are full of curl friends choosing twist outs, flat twists and braid outs to protect their scalps, maintain hair integrity and minimize breakage. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Hannah | Natural Curly Hair (@hannahmendez.x) Celebrity stylist and CEO of Texture Management, Felicia Leatherwood , knows ball when it comes to low-tension styles. Leatherwood has been mastering natural hairstyles for over 26 years and is known for Issa Rae’s soft, low-tension looks that fill our Pinterest board. Below, she spoke with ESSENCE about why you should give your hair a break this season and prioritize hair health with low tension styles this season. Curl Friends Are Letting Go Curl friends are embracing low-tension styles because they are not seen as the hairstyle you only wear running errands. These styles are worn to the office, date nights and formal gatherings. The shift is leading more people to integrate twist outs, mini braids and soft curls into their everyday routine. Low-tension styles are gaining popularity because they are approachable, healthy for the scalp and hold up well in colder temperatures when natural hair is more susceptible to breakage. “I’m seeing people wearing their hair more natural and less structured, a bit more fluffy,” Leatherwood says. “Softer curls around the face feel cozy for the winter.” Many curl friends are also experiencing thinning edges and breakage from excessive protective styling this summer. Trendy styles often require tight hair pulling and manipulation to achieve the look. Although they are cute, they come with a steep price for hair health. “At the end of the day, it’s about maintaining hair that’s healthy,” Leatherwood explains. “We need to keep it from being pulled and manipulated too much.” She looks to some of her clients like Issa Rae for inspiration. Clients who understand how to keep their hair healthy under any circumstances. “I use Issa as my template, and Beyoncé, SZA, Yara Shahidi as references,” Leatherwood says “They are doing more of that softer, low-tension looks that are easy to achieve.” These celebrities have redefined low-tension styles and made them more common on red carpets, television shows and music videos, giving curl friends the confidence to wear them too. NEW YORK, NY – SEPTEMBER 11: Yara Shahidi attends Kering Foundation Care For Women Dinner 2025 Red Carpet at The Pool on September 11, 2025 in New York. (Photo by Paul Bruinooge/Patrick McMullan via Getty Images) Low-Tension vs Protective: Know the Difference Protective styles shield the ends of your hair from daily wear and environmental damage. These styles include buns, wigs, stitch braids, updos, and sew-ins. While they do protect, many involve pulling the hair back tightly, which can sometimes create tension on the scalp. Low-tension styles leave ends exposed but reduce scalp tension. Twist outs, braid outs, Bantu knots, flat twists, and flexi rod sets all qualify—with more innovative low-tension styles being created every day. These styles are easier on the scalp, promote growth, and look natural, though they don’t last as long as high-tension styles. Leatherwood notes that some people believe pulling hair back tightly protects it, instead of protecting, it splits the ends. She recommends more low-tension styles to recover from summer’s high-tension looks. “More twist outs or perm rod curls last with the right products, look natural, and are easier on the scalp,” Leatherwood said. What Those Scalp Bumps Really Mean Tiny bumps along the hairline or base of braids are warning signs. Those high-tension hairstyles? Most are linked to traction alopecia. Studies show this type of hair loss affects one in three Black women . Leatherwood says repeated tension can also cause folliculitis, inflammation of the hair follicle. The fix is simple: avoid overly tight styles and give your scalp a break. If issues persist, consult your provider for treatments including steroids or antibiotics. She emphasizes that softer, low-tension styles give the scalp a chance to recover while keeping curls healthy and strong. How to Keep Low-Tension Styles Fresh Low-tension styles let you prioritize scalp health without sacrificing style. Leatherwood recommends products and techniques to maintain softness and curl definition. “Apply a butter or cream, massage and smooth it over the hair, then twist it,” Leatherwood says. “It keeps hair soft and reduce pulling.” Bantu knots, twist outs and flat twists keep hair healthy and cute while giving the scalp a break. For long-lasting curl sets, Leatherwood loves Ampro Curl Wax. “After curl sets, I coat the hair with it. It opens up the curls and lasts for several weeks,” Leatherwood says. Low-tension styles are ideal for the colder months, when our hair is recovering from summer styling damage and preparing for the winter frost. By letting the scalp rest and reducing tension, these styles help restore growth, maintain hair integrity—ensuring that your curls stay strong this season Low-Tension Style Inspiration If you need hair inspiration here are a few creative low-tension styles from my favorite creator curl friends that are making waves that you can share with your stylist or try at home. Written by DJ A&G Published on November 20, 2025 Share Share the post Share this link via Or copy link Copy Copied Source: Prince Williams / Getty During a recent conversation with DJ A&G, Leon Thomas opened up about how he’s balancing a busy tour schedule, a growing international fanbase, and the excitement of multiple Grammy nods — all without losing sight of the people who support him most. The singer, songwriter, producer and actor says performing for packed venues feels “even more meaningful” now that the Recording Academy has recognized his work. He also discussed his latest single, “Yes, It Is” which he co-wrote and says pulls inspiration from real-life experiences and the stories of those closest to him. ✕ From linking up with Wale in D.C. to preparing for upcoming dates in Europe and South Africa, Thomas remains focused on community. “After a 90-minute show, I’m still going to the after-party to connect with the supporters,” he shared. Between the “MUTT” remix with Chris Brown and recent collaborations like “Watching Us” with Wale, Thomas continues to show why he’s an artist built for longevity — and rooted in humility. Earlier this year, he appeared on NPR’s Tiny Desk, and when the fam at Cassius wrote about it, they noted that Thomas got his start as a Disney kid and notably landed a role on the popular Issa Rae television show Insecure . More from Cassius: With a few mixtapes under his belt, fans really began to take notice when he was credited with helping SZA develop her 2022 hit, ‘Snooze’ and also on Drake ‘s Certified Lover Boy‘s sleepy track with Lil Durk and Giveon, ‘In The Bible.’ And now, with the release of his Mutt album being hailed as one of the best and most refreshing R&B projects of 2024, he graced the famous cubicle known as NPR’s Tiny Desk , much to NPR’s surprise, as the Washington, DC, area was facing a brutal snowstorm. With a guitar strapped around his chest, he launched into compact 20-minute live performances with newer cuts like ‘Vibes Don’t Lie,’ ‘Yes It Is,’ and some sleepers from his 2023 Electric Dusk project like ‘Breaking Point’ and ‘Treasure In The Hills.’ Thomas scored big with his Billboard 100 hit “Mutt,” of which he told HuffPost, “I was nervous when we dropped [‘Mutt’] because, first off, a lot of the music wasn’t necessarily TikTok-coded. Some of the [songs] were pretty long and it was kind of fighting against the microwave generation culture of music that we’re in. Regina King will take center stage at the American Black Film Festival’s milestone 30th anniversary , serving as the 2026 festival ambassador. The 2026 ABFF, presented by Nice Crowd, will take place in Miami Beach from May 27–31 under the theme “The Homecoming,” Variety reports. King, an Oscar, Golden Globe, and Emmy-winning actor, director, and producer, will use her platform to champion the next generation of filmmakers and rising screen stars attending the annual star-studded event. As festival ambassador, King will greet attendees on opening night and headline a featured “Creator Conversation,” reflecting on her acclaimed career and ABFF’s legacy of amplifying emerging talent and highlighting film and TV projects by and about people of African descent. Her ambassadorship marks the culmination of a 30-year relationship with ABFF, dating back to its 1997 debut as the Acapulco Black Film Festival, where she first participated. “ABFF has championed countless artists and storytellers, growing into a powerful global platform,” King said in a statement. “What Jeff and Nicole Friday have built over 30 years has made a lasting impact across our industry. Returning feels like a homecoming — a celebration of our creativity, resilience, and excellence. I’m truly honored to serve as ambassador for this milestone year.” King, an Oscar winner for her performance in If Beale Street Could Talk and a four-time Primetime Emmy recipient for her work on American Crime, Seven Seconds , and Watchmen , follows a star-studded roster of ABFF ambassadors. Previous ambassadors include last year’s honorees, Nia Long and Larenz Tate, as well as Issa Rae, Lena Waithe, Halle Berry, Magic Johnson, Anthony Mackie, Common, Taye Diggs, Taraji P. Henson, Mary J. Blige, Tracee Ellis Ross, Lala Anthony, Regina Hall, Morris Chestnut, Omari Hardwick, Idris Elba, Jay Ellis, and the late John Singleton. “Regina has been part of the ABFF family since the very beginning,” said Nice Crowd CEO and Founder Jeff Friday and President Nicole Friday. “From those early years in Acapulco to everything she’s achieved since, we’ve watched her journey with so much pride — cheering her on from up close and from afar. She represents everything this festival was created to celebrate — artistry, integrity, and excellence. Having her serve as our festival ambassador for our 30th year is truly a full-circle moment and a reflection of the mutual respect and admiration we’ve shared over the years.” RELATED CONTENT: Elevating Your Excellence: The Unyielding Vision Of Pastor Jamal Bryant In The Fight For Economic And Civic Justice American Black Film Festival Regina King Subscribe to Newsletter GET THE APP About Management Masthead Privacy Policy Sales Partnership Solutions © 2025 Black Enterprise. Starting December 1 , Greta Gerwig’s bright-pink cinematic phenomenon officially lands on Tubi, making one of 2023’s biggest and most beloved films available to stream for free. Barbie became a genuine global event the moment it hit theaters, thanks to Gerwig’s clever, genre-blending direction and a cast that fully leaned into the film’s mix of satire, joy, and existential dread. The comedy holds an impressive 88% on Rotten Tomatoes and earned multiple Academy Award nominations, including one for Ryan Gosling , whose scene-stealing take on Ken became an instant pop-culture milestone. Gosling ’s performance — equal parts hilarious, unhinged, and unexpectedly emotional — turned “Ken” into both a meme and a movement. Between the Kenergy , the musical number that broke the internet ("I’m Just Ken"), and the ongoing awards-season love, his work in the film remains one of the most celebrated comedic performances in recent years. Of course, Gosling isn’t the only star in the huge ensemble cast. Margot Robbie anchors the film as Barbie, and is supported by A-listers like America Ferrera , Simu Liu , Issa Rae, Kate McKinnon, Kingsley Ben-Adir, Emma Mackey, Michael Cera, and Will Ferrell . The movie follows Barbie and Ken as they leave Barbieland for the real world — only to discover patriarchy, complicated emotions, and the horrors of corporate boardrooms. How Good Is 'Barbie'? Collider's Ross Bonaime raved about the film, labeling it as an impressive feat that manages to be wholesome while incorporating biting satire: "It’s easy to be cynical about a film like Barbie , a film that has at least partially been made to sell toys and even makes Mattel a part of the actual story. But Barbie is also an example of how getting the right people behind an unusual idea can make something truly beautiful come out of it, much like The Lego Movie or The Social Network before it. Gerwig has created a film that takes Barbie, praises its contribution as an idea to our world, but also criticizes its faults, while also making a film that celebrates being a woman and all the difficulties and beauty that includes. This also manages to be a film that feels decidedly in line with Gerwig’s previous films as she continues her streak as one of the most exciting filmmakers working today. Barbie could’ve just been a commercial, but Gerwig makes this life of plastic into something truly fantastic ." Overseen by both BUTTER executive producers Annick Mayer (West Coast North America) and Renée Massé (East Coast North America), Senécal joins the roster after working as a longtime collaborator with the studio on successful campaigns for Aveeno, Qualcomm, Juvéderm, One Love Foundation, Samsung, and more. Senécal is a classically trained pianist and a graduate of Berklee College of Music. He brings a diverse musical background to his work, weaving pop, post-modern, and contemporary influences into his classical compositions and crafting immersive sonic experiences across all media. Upon returning to BUTTER, where he first started as an intern, Senécal is poised to make a significant impact on the company’s Canadian operations. Massé noted, “When I started at BUTTER six years ago, David was one of my first interns, and he immediately caught my attention with his passion, creativity, kindness, and talent. Given Annick and my French-Canadian roots, expanding into Québec and Canada has forever been a dream for BUTTER, and I’ve always known David would be the one to make that dream a reality with.” Senécal added, “Joining Butter in this new chapter feels like coming home. I started my career here years ago, and now I get to help grow its presence in the Canadian market–surrounded by so many artists and creatives I admire. It’s a chance to keep telling stories through sound, but on a bigger scale.” Before joining BUTTER, Senécal honed his craft at Studio BULLDOG, working with Canadian brands such as Fido, Brunet, BELL, Cozey, and Opera, among others. Beyond branded content, Senécal’s work spans 30 audiobooks, numerous television shows, short film The Bingo Sisters (2024), and feature-length film Talk Soon (2020), directed by Joey Massa. Talk Soon screened at the Boden International Film Festival, Queer Film Festival, and Carmarthen Bay Film Festival, winning awards at each of these venues and several others. Additionally, he co-scored the feature film Lovely Day (2025) with Martin Leon, which premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival. As a multifaceted artist, he also writes and performs his own music under the moniker MERLYN. While building upon this collection of compositions and scores for fellow Canadian artists, he has amassed a network of international vocal and musician talent that will reinforce BUTTER’s expanding roster. By Zara Amaechi Arts Access Reporter Nov. 13, 2025 | Updated 5:30 p.m. CST | 3 min. read Showcasing Black-Owned Brands panel discussion during Day 4 of the American Black Film Festival on June 14, 2025 in Miami Beach, FL. Kelvin Bulluck / Kelvin Bulluck / Nice Crowd The American Black Film Festival, known for launching the careers of filmmakers including Ryan Coogler, Issa Rae and Ava DuVernay, is bringing its first ever two-day pop-up event to Dallas this weekend at AMC NorthPark 15. The American Black Film Festival launched in 1997 to provide opportunities to emerging artists and talented people who don’t have access to the industry. The ABFF Pop Up Tour will offer film screenings, celebrity conversations and a masterclass for aspiring creatives. The tour is part of a new national initiative by Nice Crowd, the event company behind the 30-year-old film festival. The event also serves as a lead-up to the 30th anniversary celebration of ABFF next May in Miami Beach, Fla. Nicole Friday, president and co-founder of Nice Crowd, said the pop-ups expand access to the industry for storytellers who may not be able to attend the main event in Florida. SIGN UP Or with: Google By signing up, you agree to our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. “We wanted to really bring some of the same energy and excitement of the festival to four cities where we could celebrate culture and creativity with regional talent and connect them to national industry opportunities,” Friday said. Advertisement The tour launched in New York last month, continued in Atlanta and will wrap up in Los Angeles in December. Including Dallas in the lineup, Friday said, was intentional. “It’s a vibrant creative hub,” she said. “Dallas folks have been asking for us to bring a little bit of ABFF to the city, and so we’re excited to be in Dallas.” Advertisement Showcasing Black-Owned Brands panel discussion during Day 4 of the American Black Film Festival on June 14, 2025 in Miami Beach, FL. Kelvin Bulluck / Kelvin Bulluck / Nice Crowd Advertisement The two-day event will feature a masterclass presented by the New York Film Academy called “Break It Down: How to Bring Any Script to Life,” taught by actor Gerrard James. It will also include a conversation on sports and storytelling with WNBA stars Syd Colson and Theresa “TP” Plaisance. The HBO Short Film Showcase on Saturday will spotlight five finalists from this year’s ABFF, followed by a discussion panel with filmmakers Princess Adenike and Sam Henderson. On Sunday, attendees can catch several independent films and award-winning shorts, including The Fisherman , winner of best narrative feature and best director at the 2025 ABFF, and Fatherless No More , a documentary about a former NFL player turned pastor mentoring inmates at Riker Island. Advertisement “If you are a writer, actor, there’s a masterclass. if you’re a film connoisseur and you love independent films, there’s something for you,” Friday said. “If you want to know about sports and the business of sports, I think there’s something for that audience as well.” Details: Nov. 15-16. 11 a.m. AMC NorthPark 15, 8687 N Central Expy #3000, Dallas. Tickets range from $15-$30 based on each event. (Disney/Jose Alvarado) Teyana Taylor is no stranger to the public eye, but with several films now under her belt, she says it’s pretty difficult to be a Black woman in Hollywood. “The hardest part is being a woman in Hollywood,” she tells Elle . “The even harder part is being a Black woman in Hollywood, because I do feel like this is a man’s world. And we have to show who we are as women to be respected in that space.” Despite the hardships, she says she does see “change happening” and “more light being shed on women.” “I think it’s because we’re busting through the doors, unapologetically us. We’re not giving anybody a choice: you will see us and you will hear us. And if you don’t, we’re going to make you,” Teyana says. “Seeing women step into our glory and standing 10 toes down in some red bottoms has been amazing. We’re really stomping through, and that’s what I love about being a woman in Hollywood. We’re going to make you hear us.” In her own journey, she credits women like Taraji P. Henson , Sarah Paulson , Niecy Nash , Issa Rae , Kerry Washington and Regina Hall for showing up for her. “To be able to call on my village, and then they all show up in a heartbeat, no hesitation, feels good,” Teyana tells Elle . “Their support felt like a comforting hug that whispered, ‘Mm-hmm, it’s okay. We got you.'” “To see such beautiful women who have overcome so much and kept their crowns lifted through it all, show up for me. It really, really meant a lot,” she continues. And we have to show who we are as women to be respected in that space. ” Despite the hardships, she says she does see “change happening” and “more light being shed on women. ” “I think it’s because we’re busting through the doors, unapologetically us. We’re not giving anybody a choice: you will see us and you will hear us. And if you don’t, we’re going to make you,” Teyana says. “Seeing women step into our glory and standing 10 toes down in some red bottoms has been amazing. We’re really stomping through, and that’s what I love about being a woman in Hollywood. We’re going to make you hear us. ” In her own journey, she credits women like Taraji P. Henson , Sarah Paulson , Niecy Nash , Issa Rae , Kerry Washington and Regina Hall for showing up for her. “To be able to call on my village, and then they all show up in a heartbeat, no hesitation, feels good,” Teyana tells Elle. “Their support felt like a comforting hug that whispered, ‘Mm-hmm, it’s okay. '” “To see such beautiful women who have overcome so much and kept their crowns lifted through it all, show up for me. It really, really meant a lot,” she continues. The full interview, in which Teyana also opens up about her experience in culinary school, is live on Elle

(Disney/Jose Alvarado) Teyana Taylor is no stranger to the public eye, but with several films now under her belt, she says it’s pretty difficult to be a Black woman in Hollywood. “The hardest part is being a woman in Hollywood,” she tells Elle. “The even harder part is being a Black woman in Hollywood, because I do feel like this is a man’s world. And we have to show who we are as women to be respected in that space. ” Despite the hardships, she says she does see “change happening” and “more light being shed on women. ” “I think it’s because we’re busting through the doors, unapologetically us. We’re not giving anybody a choice: you will see us and you will hear us. And if you don’t, we’re going to make you,” Teyana says. “Seeing women step into our glory and standing 10 toes down in some red bottoms has been amazing. We’re really stomping through, and that’s what I love about being a woman in Hollywood. We’re going to make you hear us. ” In her own journey, she credits women like Taraji P. Henson , Sarah Paulson , Niecy Nash , Issa Rae , Kerry Washington and Regina Hall for showing up for her. “To be able to call on my village, and then they all show up in a heartbeat, no hesitation, feels good,” Teyana tells Elle. “Their support felt like a comforting hug that whispered, ‘Mm-hmm, it’s okay. '” “To see such beautiful women who have overcome so much and kept their crowns lifted through it all, show up for me. It really, really meant a lot,” she continues. The full interview, in which Teyana also opens up about her experience in culinary school, is live on Elle

(Photos © HBO Max) HBO recently announced the renewal of two Game Of Thrones spinoffs, A Knight Of The Seven Kingdoms and House Of The Dragon, extending each series to 2028. Both shows will be available to stream on HBO Max. The first half-hour episode of A Knight Of The Seven Kingdoms will be released on Jan 19. The second season will debut in 2027. The third season of House Of The Dragon will debut next year and the fourth season will stream in 2028. "Together, House Of The Dragon and A Knight Of The Seven Kingdoms reveal just how expansive and richly imagined George R.R. Martin's universe continues to be," said Francesca Orsi of HBO. "In January, I think audiences will be delighted by the inspiring underdog tale of Dunk and Egg that George and Ira Parker have so beautifully captured. And House Of The Dragon is set to ignite once again with some of its most epic battles yet." A Knight Of The Seven Kingdoms, set in the world of Westeros, is an endearing tale centred on the adventures of an unexpected duo. Season 1's cast includes Peter Claffey as Ser Duncan "Dunk" the Tall and Dexter Sol Ansell as Egg, and is directed by Owen Harris and Sarah Adina Smith. Based on George R.R. Martin's Fire & Blood, House Of The Dragon, set 200 years before the events of Game Of Thrones, tells the story of House Targaryen. Season 3's cast includes Matt Smith, Emma D'Arcy and Olivia Cooke. text: House of the Dragon Season 3 Could Feature This Character From Daemon’s Vision Skip to content ComingSoon.net - Movie Trailers, TV & Streaming News, and More Open Close Menu Open menu Streaming Schedules Apple TV+ Disney+ Hulu Max Netflix Paramount+ Peacock Prime Video Open menu Movies Movie News Movie Features Movie Reviews Open menu TV TV News TV Features TV Reviews Open menu Games Video Game News Video Game Features Video Game Reviews Trailers Open menu Genres Anime Collectibles Comics Documentaries Family Horror Sci-Fi Wrestling Facebook Instagram Twitter Search Close Search Image credit: HBO TV House of the Dragon Season 3 Could Feature This Character From Daemon’s Vision October 29, 2025 By Evolve Editors Newly surfaced set photos from House of the Dragon Season 3 have sparked fan speculation after revealing a mysterious figure in green makeup and forest-like attire. The images suggest the possible introduction of the Green Men, the mythical guardians from George R.R. Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire. House of the Dragon Season 3 set photos hint at debut of Isle of Faces’ Green Men Set photos from the third season of House of the Dragon have offered a closer look at an important addition to the Game of Thrones universe. The images, reportedly taken from the production set, appear to show the Green Men, figures from George R.R. Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire lore. The HBO series, based on Martin’s Fire & Blood, will continue to follow the Targaryen civil war known as the Dance of the Dragons. In the newly surfaced photos, an actor can be seen wearing green prosthetics. He was in a costume designed with forest-like details, including prominent antlers. This has led to speculation that the character represents one of the Green Men, who briefly appeared in Season 2. In that earlier sequence, Daemon Targaryen followed Alys Rivers to the Godswood at Harrenhal. In that scene, Daemon briefly encountered a shadowed figure resembling a Green Man before experiencing his prophetic vision of the war’s outcome. View this post on Instagram A post shared by House of the Dragon (@houseofthedragoons) Within Martin’s story, the Green Men are described as guardians of the Isle of Faces, a sacred location in the center of the Gods Eye lake. The island is home to ancient weirwood trees, believed to hold deep spiritual significance. House of the Dragon Season 3 has wrapped filming, with the series expected to return to HBO Max following post-production. It will continue to explore the ongoing conflict between the Greens and the Blacks of House Targaryen. The series’ cast includes Matt Smith, Emma D’Arcy, and Olivia Cooke, among many others. The Devil's Hour View full post on YouTube The Times praised the first six-part series of this drama, starring Peter Capaldi as a serial killer, as presenting: “an ordinary world tinged with nightmares and the possibility of encroaching madness”. Sounds pretty decent, right? Jessica Raine is the social worker who wakes mysteriously at 3:33 every morning, experiencing nightmarish visions that seem to connect her to a recent string of brutal events. If you like what you see, a second series was released last year. 2. Fear View full post on YouTube This recent Glasgow-set thriller starring The Line of Duty ’s Martin Compston and Anjli Mohindra was described as “extraordinarily creepy” by the Guardian , and, as the three-parter based on the novel by Dirk Kurbjuweit unfolds, it proves exactly that. A couple move into a new home and discover that their basement neighbour is at the troublingly extreme end of “friendly”. But does he have a tragic past of his own that he’s reckoning with? What to Read Next 3. The Girlfriend Robin Wright’s Laura loves her adult son, Daniel (Laurie Davidson). No no, really loves him, so that when Daniel brings home a new girlfriend, who could just be the one. But Daniel’s new squeeze, Cherry (Olivia Cooke), may also have an agenda of her own, and not be exactly who she seems. No wonder Variety called it “wickedly intriguing” and “a wild, thrilling ride”. 4. The Assassin View full post on YouTube Family drama meets brutal crime in this recent six-parter , which stars Keeley Hawes as an assassin who is forced out of retirement – like Malice , it begins in Greece, where Hawes’ Julie is holed up – while also navigating a tricky relationship with her long-lost son, Edward (Freddie Highmore). There’s comedy as well as intrigue, and unsurprisingly the Irish Independent called it “terrific fun”. 5. Lazarus View full post on YouTube We’d watch Bill Nighy filing his tax return, so the fact that he stars in this twisty Harlan Coben thriller about father-and-son psychiatrists, starring Sam Claflin as the son, is absolutely fine by us. That it takes a supernatural turn is also perfectly OK – Claflin’s character is visited by the ghosts of his Nighy’s characters patients – and when the Financial Times calls it “silly yet watchable” we remain absolutely sold. Though this fantasy series has been an overall success, it hasn't avoided the obligatory criticisms that have traditionally plagued book-to-screen adaptations. HBO has taken significant creative liberties with George R.R. Martin's Westeros history , some of which the author himself has criticized. Rhaenyra's character, played by Emma D'Arcy, is at the center of many of House of the Dragon 's biggest changes. In Martin's Fire & Blood , this queen was referred to as Rhaenyra the Cruel. She certainly wasn't the worst Targaryen ruler, but this highly moral and relatively blameless figure we see in House of the Dragon isn't how she was remembered in Westeros. Additionally, we see Rhaenyra express a desire to fight in season 2, a change that House of the Dragon ​​​​​​season 3 seems to have run with. Rhaenyra's Sword Is Front And Center In House Of The Dragon Season 3's Marketing Emma D'Arcy as Rhaenyra Targaryen wielding a sword in House of the Dragon season 2 We knew that Rhaenyra would likely have a sword in House of the Dragon season 3, since D'Arcy revealed to Josh Horowitz on the Happy Sad Confused podcast that they had asked Ryan Condal to allow their character to carry one. It sounded as if this wasn't for the purpose of fighting. Rather, like the male characters, D'Arcy would have a place to place their hands during scenes. It's a gesture that implies authority and makes some sense for the Queen of Westeros. Interestingly, a new promotional poster for House of the Dragon season 3 sees Rhaenyra not just holding a sword as she has in the past, but brandishing it. This implies that we will actually see D'Arcy's character in combat. Furthermore, the sword's feature in promotional material indicates that Rhaenyra's use of the weapon will be central in the coming episodes. It's a sign that House of the Dragon is committing to its Rhaenyra changes. How Rhaenyra Having A Sword Changes Her Character From The Book There's been a lot of debate since the House of the Dragon marketing materials began circulating on the internet about whether book Rhaenyra carried a sword. Discovering the definitive truth is tricky, since Fire & Blood doesn't have a traditional narrative like the other A Song of Ice and Fire books do. Instead, this tome is structured like a found manuscript, written by Martin but credited to the in-world character of Archmaester Gyldayn. Though we don't get any POV narrative in Fire & Blood , the battles, in particular, are described in significant detail. It's very clear that Gyldayn didn't believe that Rhaenyra had taken part in combat. Her role was purely royal and strategic. While other dragon riders, like Rhaenys, did fight and die in battle, Rhaenyra only rode into King's Landing on Syrax to take the throne, not to fight to claim the city. She wasn't a warrior. Still, official art for Fire & Blood shows Rhaenyra with a sword on her belt, which is why many have argued that a sword for D'Arcy isn't a change. Still, this art never shows Rhaenyra brandishing the sword as she does in the promotional material. More likely, it's a symbolic weapon—something to relay her power. No matter how you slice it, the idea of Rhaenyra in combat isn't something that comes directly from Martin himself. Why Rhaenyra's Sword Is House Of The Dragon Is Not A Big Deal Though we can confirm that Rhaenyra's sword in House of the Dragon season 3 is a change from the books, the real question here is whether it matters. This Game of Thrones spinoff has a unique advantage over its predecessor. As previously mentioned, Martin wrote Fire & Blood as if it were a sort of historical tome written by a Maester. Gyldayn did not witness any of the events from the Dance of the Dragons. Instead, he researched the conflicts of the Targaryen civil war and recorded them. This detail gives the showrunners of House of the Dragon an advantage. They've leaned into the " unreliable narrator " trope, painting Rhaenyra as a queen somewhat misunderstood by history. To a point, this makes sense. It's fun and interesting to see HBO's version of what really happened and how that differs from how Westeros would remember her. This same justification could be used for Rhaenyra's use of a sword in House of the Dragon season 3. Of course, this doesn't mean that House of the Dragon can do anything it wants with Martin's story. The author himself has been critical of changes, and his opinion is what really matters, said and done. As an audience, we can sit back and see precisely how HBO uses Rhaenyra and her sword in the coming episodes. Bassyonni 27 Nov 2025 Home News Sports Entertainment Tech Business Home Entertainment ‘House of the Dragon’ Secures Renewal for Exciting Season 4 Entertainment ‘House of the Dragon’ Secures Renewal for Exciting Season 4 Bassyonni ago 6 days “House of the Dragon” has officially secured a renewal for Season 4, with its debut expected in 2028. This announcement came during an HBO press presentation in New York. The highly anticipated third season is set to premiere in summer 2026. Exciting News for Fans The renewal not only boosts the excitement for “House of the Dragon,” but it also extends the “Game of Thrones” universe. HBO CEO Casey Bloys confirmed that another prequel, “A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms,” has also been renewed for a second season. This second season is scheduled for release in 2027, ensuring fans will have fresh content from Westeros annually through 2028. About “House of the Dragon” Inspired by George R. R. Martin’s book “Fire & Blood,” “House of the Dragon” takes viewers on a journey 200 years prior to the events of “Game of Thrones.” The series follows the Targaryen lineage, showcasing events that unfold before the birth of iconic characters like Daenerys Targaryen. Cast and Crew The cast includes notable actors such as: Matt Smith Emma D’Arcy Olivia Cooke Steve Toussaint Rhys Ifans Fabien Frankel Ewan Mitchell Harry Collett Others include: Tom Glynn-Carney, Bethany Antonia, Phoebe Campbell, and more. The series creator and showrunner, Ryan Condal, is joined by co-creator George R. R. Martin and several executive producers, including Sara Hess and Melissa Bernstein. Plans for the Future Francesca Orsi, HBO’s EVP of programming, expressed enthusiasm about delivering new seasons of both “House of the Dragon” and “A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms.” She highlighted the richness of Martin’s universe, stating it would captivate audiences in the upcoming seasons. This summer’s “House of the Dragon” is expected to feature some of its most thrilling battles, promising an exciting continuation of this epic saga. Now five seasons deep, Slow Horses is one of the best spy thrillers on TV today. Following the antics of the parents relegated to Slough House, home to the disgraced and failed agents of MI5, a life of the mundane is anything but. What makes Slow Horses so bingeable is the agents who work inside . With a major delineation between Slough House and MI5 and the Dogs, just because you're a Slow Horse doesn't mean you're not an eccentric and enigmatic character . We're here to rank our Slough House agents based on their personality, success as an agent, and character profile. Each Slow Horse has something unique they bring to the table , but who's the best of all time? 12 Catherine Standish Played by Saskia Reeves Saskia Reeves as Catherine Standish playing chess in Slow Horses. Image via Apple TV Justice for Standish! Now listen, Catherine Standish ( Saskia Reeves ) technically isn't a field agent, but Slough House would simply be unable to function without her . Even when she was gone and Moira Tregorian ( Joanna Scanlan ) took over, Slough House was just not the same. We are honoring her because if we're basing Slough House based on accountability, she tops the list. But then again, the bar is low. These agents are here for a reason. Nevertheless, it's time for Standish's highlight reel. As the office administrator, Standish tends to be more in tune with everything than anyone. With experience in field interrogations and hostage negotiations, Standish can apply those skills when least expected . Her biggest flaw is her suffering from alcoholism. Almost blinded by her former employer, Charles Partner ( James Faulkner ), it often puts her at odds with Jackson Lamb ( Gary Oldman ), despite her undying loyalty to him. And their reliance on one another, ultimately, is why Slough House is even still standing. Saskia Reeves does a remarkable job of bringing Standish to life . Meek and reserved, she knows when to turn it on and bring Standish's skills to the forefront. 11 Jed Moody Played by Steven Waddington Steven Waddington as Jed Moody looking down on 'Slow Horses.' Image via Apple TV Some people don't like working at Slough House. Like they really hate it. A former member of the Dogs under Nick Duffy ( Chris Reilly ), Jed Moody ( Steven Waddington ) was willing to go to great lengths to get out of Slough House. Even betray Jackson Lamb to do so. A former tactical operative, Moody was exiled from the Park following a failed operation that resulted in the loss of a massive sum of money for MI5. At Slough House, Moody goes rogue, hoping to get in the good graces of Deputy Director General Diana Taverner ( Kristin Scott Thomas ) by admitting he bugged Lamb's office in order to produce incriminating evidence. He then compromises the mission to get evidence on Robert Hobden ( Paul Hilton ) and ultimately kills him. And then it all goes down from there. Moody's downfall was, well, a fall down . After returning to Slough House to remove the bug, he unexpectedly gets into a scuffle with Min Harper ( Dustin Demri-Burns ) and Louisa Guy ( Rosalind Eleazar ). The skirmish does not go off without a hitch; he and Min end up falling down the stairs during the struggle, causing Moody to break his neck. Portrayed by Steven Waddington, Moody had the shortest tenure of a Slough House agent in the series. 10 Struan Loy Played by Paul Higgins Paul Higgins as Struan Loy looking sullen on 'Slow Horses.' Image via Apple TV If there's one thing you should never do, it's betray Jackson Lamb. Unfortunately for Struan Loy ( Paul Higgins ), that was his gravest mistake. After sending an inappropriate email about his boss, Loy was assigned to Slough House. Peppy and quite chatty, Loy was fine at his job . Some of his cohorts found him a tad annoying, but that didn't mean he was a foul agent. What he was not great at was crafting solid ideas that wouldn't ultimately result in his dismissal from the dredges at Slough House. Loy is relentless and eager to get back to the Park. He ends up spilling the beans to Deputy Director General Diana Taverner about a potential connection between Jackson Lamb and Sons of Albion's Alan Black ( Sam Hazeldine ). Lamb knows it came from Loy, and when the dust settles, given the option to take him back, Lamb refuses, telling Taverner to throw him into the wilderness, never to be seen again. If we follow the books, we may not have seen the last of Loy , played with heart by Paul Higgins. In fact, he technically does return in the seventh book, only to be swiftly murdered. Nevertheless, it would be nice to see him return for another go at it. 9 Marcus Longridge Played by Kadiff Kirwan Kadiff Kirwan as Marcus Longridge sitting with arms crossed on 'Slow Horses.' Image via Apple TV Once a tactical agent for MI5, Marcus Longridge ( Kadiff Kirwan ) was bogged down by a severe gambling addiction. He is a capable and strong agent, but being tied to Shirley Dander ( Aimee-Ffion Edwards ) was a cog in his downfall. Spoiler alert. The married father brought a lot of heart to Slough House, but his addiction became his main issue, affecting every aspect of his life . As much as he tried to fight the addiction, he was never fully in a position to beat it. As one of the most proficient in combat and weapons, Marcus is great in the field. As one half of the Laurel and Hardy of Slough House, it was Marcus and Shirley all the time. Whether joining forces on the field or spending endless episodes pondering if they're getting fired, it wasn't until Season 4 that Marcus broke out. Sadly, his gambling debt got the best of him , and when his gun, which became his Chekov's gun, was introduced into the story, it was only a matter of time before it would end up letting him down. Played by Kadiff Kirwan, perhaps Marcus is best remembered for his latter run in the series, but as an overall character, he sadly was only supplementary. 8 Shirley Dander Played by Aimee-Ffion Edwards Aimee-Ffion Edwards as Shirley with wet hair looks ahead with a serious expression in Slow Horses. Image via Apple TV We could easily just pair Shirley and Marcus together, but one's alive and the other is dead. So, I think that speaks for the slight edge given to Shirley. To be frank, the dynamic duo have been my least favorite additions to the story, making me wonder, could Slow Horses exist without them? The answer is very likely, but Shirley is the less interesting of the duo, as Marcus has a more intriguing backstory. Nevertheless, let's discuss Shirley. The queen of drug and anger issues, Shirley joins Slough House after punching a superior . See! Anger issues. Nevertheless, what she brings to the team is good instincts. What she does not bring to the team is being able to apprehend a target. Shirley is the epitome of someone who needs a partner despite being able to work with one. Shirley is completely unpredictable, which is not an asset at all. What she lacks in skills she makes up for in confidence. Aimee-Ffion Edwards does a solid job playing Shirley, even if the show doesn't propel her to a top spot. That said, her banter with Marcus shows that co-workers can be platonic and have deep respect for one another . It's just a shame how co-dependent they were. Their personal addictions helped their connection, but they simply were not the best person to be in one another's lives. 7 Min Harper Played by Dustin Demri-Burns Dustin Demri-Burns as Min Harper on 'Slow Horses. Image via Apple TV Some people are subjected to Slough House because of bone-headed moves. Such was the case for Min Harper. After losing a highly classified disk on a train, Min received his demotion, and this ruined his life and marriage . The "Butt-Monkey" of Slough House, he's well-meaning but a clumsy guy on the job. He's got a beautiful heart and even helps alleviate the doom and gloom. Like most shows, there needs to be some romance, and since Min was single and ready to mingle, he had a romance blossom with Louisa Guy . Now, we all know what happens when love fills the air in a crime thriller. Especially when they know too much. Assigned to trail Russian Oligarch, Arkady Pashkin ( Alec Utgoff ) under the request of James "Spider" Webb ( Freddie Fox ), Min and Louisa get a bit too close to Pashkin's bodyguards' instincts. What was deemed an accident was anything but . It's never easy to lose a beloved character, but for Min, he was a casualty of the story. Dustin Demri-Burns was quite phenomenal as Min. It's why his untimely death stung. 6 Roddy Ho Played by Christopher Chung Christopher Chung in "Slow Horses," now streaming on Apple TV+. Image via Apple TV What Roddy Ho (Christopher Chung) is good at is technology and being the comic relief . The end . No, I kid. Roddy is an arrogant and obnoxious tech nerd who feels most at home in front of a screen . As a former hacktivist, Roddy is a major asset to Slough House, as there's no one else on the team with his skills. Now, do not ask him to go out into the field, because chances are he'll botch the mission. Though some may consider him useless, without him, many necessary technical maneuvers would never have happened. Shockingly, not a main cast member until Season 5, Christopher Chung has been more than a co-star ; he was the other side of Jackson Lamb's humor. When things get heavy, we turn to Roddy for a hearty laugh and a good chuckle as a reminder that we're not him . Roddy is one of the most complete characters in the ensemble. Protect Roddy at all costs! 5 Sid Baker Played by Olivia Cooke A close up of Olivia Cooke with her hair up and looking at someone off-camera in Slow Horses. Image via Apple TV When you realize that Olivia Cooke , future star of House of the Dragon , was only a single-season player, it might surprise you. But her turn as Sid Baker was crucial to the overall arc of Slow Horses . Unfortunately, as the show progressed, Sid seems to have been lost in memory; she was essentially a strong agent. With remarkable in-field intuition, her undercover prowess to uncover far-right-wing journalist Robert Hobden proved her worth. Her strong skills of deception earned her praise from Lamb , proving she could handle covert operations. Sid is quite brilliant, yet often has to keep her intelligence in check. Especially around River Cartwright ( Jack Lowden ). Sid seemed like she was destined to be solely an eventual love interest for River, so maybe it was best to kill her off early. Except, is Sid really dead? Could her alleged death and complete identity have been scrubbed, and she's still looming out there? It would be a lovely shock for Sid to have faked her death . To see Sid return would be a lovely twist! 4 J.K. Coe Played by Tom Brooke Tom Brooke as JK Coe wearing a hoodie and observing in Slow Horses. Image via Apple TV Many agents on this list might be mad at J.K. Coe ( Tom Brooke ) for swooping in and dropping them down a spot on this list. But the mysterious agent, who joined in Season 4, has already made a name for himself as a top agent . Where he lacks in social skills, he makes up for it in intuition, intelligence, and stealth . Having an innate skill of perception, Coe has been a valuable asset thus far. Physically, a major asset to the team, Coe seems to be someone who should top the list, but after being kidnapped, his trauma continues to hold him back. In his eyes, everything is a weapon. When it came to the later additions to the cast, Tom Brooke brought much-needed new energy to the group. Even with a character who lacks emotion and loves to wear his hood up, Brooke is able to build a fascinating character with very little runway to work with . It's fascinating to watch. For an individual dealing with psychological trauma, Brooke allows Coe's panic attacks as a sort of badge of honor. Where Brooke does add color is his contact ribbing of Roddy. Coe is easily the most interesting character, with so much more room to grow. He's growing into one of the most crucial players on the team. 3 Louisa Guy Played by Rosalind Eleazar Louisa (Rosalind Eleazar) sitting with legs crouched on a bench outside in 'Slow Horses'. Image via Apple TV Perhaps she could be a spot higher if she were presented as the lead , but nevertheless, Louisa Guy is one of the best at Slough House. After a tail operation went badly, Louisa was relegated to Slough House, determined to right her wrong. She is a level-headed agent who understands what it means to be a good agent. She was the de facto leader until River dropped in , yet she's still the strongest in the field. One of her greatest attributes is her ability to pick up the slack for her fellow Slow Horses, which stems from her ability to act under pressure. With a brilliant mind for critical thinking? It's a bit unfair to understate Louisa, just as it is to underestimate Rosalind Eleazar's performance . She served as a romantically tinged character in the first part of her journey, but after Min was killed, Louisa changed, allowing Eleazar to discover a new side of her. In a way, it built Louisa as an agent while simultaneously breaking her . Grief can do impossible things, but for Louisa, she's forced to face her trauma head-on. If there's one individual who might return to MI5, it's Louisa. Google is updating how content is shown. Protect Roddy at all costs! 5 Sid Baker Played by Olivia Cooke A close up of Olivia Cooke with her hair up and looking at someone off-camera in Slow Horses. Image via Apple TV When you realize that Olivia Cooke , future star of House of the Dragon , was only a single-season player, it might surprise you. But her turn as Sid Baker was crucial to the overall arc of Slow Horses. Unfortunately, as the show progressed, Sid seems to have been lost in memory; she was essentially a strong agent. With remarkable in-field intuition, her undercover prowess to uncover far-right-wing journalist Robert Hobden proved her worth. Her strong skills of deception earned her praise from Lamb , proving she could handle covert operations. Sid is quite brilliant, yet often has to keep her intelligence in check. Especially around River Cartwright ( Jack Lowden ). Sid seemed like she was destined to be solely an eventual love interest for River, so maybe it was best to kill her off early. Except, is Sid really dead? Could her alleged death and complete identity have been scrubbed, and she's still looming out there? It would be a lovely shock for Sid to have faked her death. To see Sid return would be a lovely twist! 4 J. Coe Played by Tom Brooke Tom Brooke as JK Coe wearing a hoodie and observing in Slow Horses. Image via Apple TV Many agents on this list might be mad at J. Coe ( Tom Brooke ) for swooping in and dropping them down a spot on this list. But the mysterious agent, who joined in Season 4, has already made a name for himself as a top agent. Where he lacks in social skills, he makes up for it in intuition, intelligence, and stealth. Having an innate skill of perception, Coe has been a valuable asset thus far. Physically, a major asset to the team, Coe seems to be someone who should top the list, but after being kidnapped, his trauma continues to hold him back. In his eyes, everything is a weapon. When it came to the later additions to the cast, Tom Brooke brought much-needed new energy to the group. Even with a character who lacks emotion and loves to wear his hood up, Brooke is able to build a fascinating character with very little runway to work with. For an individual dealing with psychological trauma, Brooke allows Coe's panic attacks as a sort of badge of honor. Where Brooke does add color is his contact ribbing of Roddy. Coe is easily the most interesting character, with so much more room to grow. He's growing into one of the most crucial players on the team. 3 Louisa Guy Played by Rosalind Eleazar Louisa (Rosalind Eleazar) sitting with legs crouched on a bench outside in 'Slow Horses'. Image via Apple TV Perhaps she could be a spot higher if she were presented as the lead , but nevertheless, Louisa Guy is one of the best at Slough House. After a tail operation went badly, Louisa was relegated to Slough House, determined to right her wrong. She is a level-headed agent who understands what it means to be a good agent. She was the de facto leader until River dropped in , yet she's still the strongest in the field. One of her greatest attributes is her ability to pick up the slack for her fellow Slow Horses, which stems from her ability to act under pressure. With a brilliant mind for critical thinking? It's a bit unfair to understate Louisa, just as it is to underestimate Rosalind Eleazar's performance. She served as a romantically tinged character in the first part of her journey, but after Min was killed, Louisa changed, allowing Eleazar to discover a new side of her. In a way, it built Louisa as an agent while simultaneously breaking her. Grief can do impossible things, but for Louisa, she's forced to face her trauma head-on. If there's one individual who might return to MI5, it's Louisa. Google is updating how content is shown. text: Blacktop International takes worldwide rights to Kurt Martin's 'The Room Below' as production wraps in Sydney - IF Magazine News Film Festivals Box Office TV & Streaming Online Games Business Distribution and Sales Marketing Funding Professional Development Awards Tech Videos New Zealand In Production Advertise Reading Blacktop International takes worldwide rights to Kurt Martin’s ‘The Room Below’ as production wraps in Sydney Share Tweet ADVERTISEMENT Blacktop International takes worldwide rights to Kurt Martin’s ‘The Room Below’ as production wraps in Sydney Sean Slatter · Film News · November 12, 2025 Alyssa Sutherland and Jonathan Rhys Meyers. International sales company Blacktop International has acquired worldwide rights to writer/director Kurt Martin’s psychological creature horror The Room Below , which has wrapped production in Sydney. Martin’s second feature stars Alyssa Sutherland as Mia, an acclaimed children’s book author grieving the loss of her son, who forms a connection with a young boy (Gilbert Bradman) who bears a resemblance to the child she lost. But as a mysterious creature begins to stir within her home and strange events grow harder to explain, her fragile sense of reality draws the attention of a retired detective (Jonathan Rhys Meyers) searching for answers of his own. Bobby Gilchrist, Lauren Grimson, and Goran D. Kleut round out the cast. The film is produced by Jim Robison of Lunar Pictures, Chris Chard of CME, and Ty Linegar, with Marc Furmie, Colin Bates, William Ramsey, Adam Cullen, Phil Hunt, Compton Ross, Roy Scott MacFarland, Samuel A. Levine, and Jaime King executive producing. Gilbert Bradman and Alyssa Sutherland. Blacktop International, led by JD Beauﬁls, will introduce the film to buyers at this year’s American Film Market (AFM) ahead of a 2026 release date. Martin and Robison said they were pleased to collaborate with Beauﬁls and Blacktop International on the project. “Their passion and reach make them the ideal team to bring The Room Below to audiences worldwide,” they said. Beaufils said his involvement in the film came after seeing some of the early footage at last year’s AFM. “I first came across The Room Below exactly a year ago at AFM in 2024 and when I got the chance to meet Jim and look at some of the footage I made it a priority of acquiring a film that marries the best elements of an elevated psychological horror that goes to frighteningly dark places, has stellar performances by well-known cast and also expert filmmaking from visionary director Kurt Martin,” he said. It is one of multiple upcoming projects for Lunar Pictures , based in Byron Bay, which is also producing Anton Corbijn’s Switzerland , starring Helen Mirren, Alden Ehrenreich, and Olivia Cooke.
