In an interview, the actress responded to audience discussions and fan art imagining her as Wonder Woman or Catwoman. The conversation reignited interest in the DCU’s upcoming projects under Gunn’s “Gods and Monsters” chapter. Alexandra Daddario hasn’t seen any of her Wonder Woman fan art Alexandra Daddario recently addressed speculation about her potential involvement in James Gunn’s DC Universe during an interview with ScreenRant . While promoting her new film, I Wish You All The Best, Alexandra Daddario addressed fan art that depicts her as Wonder Woman or Catwoman, two roles audiences have imagined her playing in the new DCU. “I have to be honest, I haven’t seen any of that [fan art],” she said. She added, “I’m flattered to hear that it’s happening, but I haven’t seen it,” noting she wasn’t aware of the fan casting. When the interviewer asked if she would join Gunn’s DC Universe, Daddario replied, “Of course, working with James Gunn would be amazing in any capacity, but I wasn’t aware that that was going on.” Both Wonder Woman and Catwoman will appear in upcoming DCU projects. Gunn revealed on Threads on September 29, 2025, that Catwoman will appear in the franchise, though her specific project remains unannounced. Meanwhile, the Wonder Woman feature film entered early development in June 2025, with Supergirl: Woman of Tomorrow writer Ana Nogueira set to pen the script. Additionally, a prequel series titled Paradise Lost remains in slow development. Gunn told Entertainment Weekly that it is “moving,” but the project does not yet have a finalized creative team. While fans continue to share casting theories, DC Studios has not announced any actors for its Wonder Woman reboot. If the script progresses as planned, industry speculation suggests a possible release window around 2028. Despite their efforts to stay an anonymous entity among their classmates, Ben begins to grow close with Nathan, a charismatic classmate for whom they develop feelings, and Ms. Lyons, the school's art teacher who works to help Ben unlock their creativity and help them process their turbulent family situation. Tommy Dorfman, best known for her acting work in Netflix's 13 Reasons Why and The CW's Jane the Virgin , makes her feature directorial debut on I Wish You All The Best and has assembled a star-studded roster for it. My Life with the Walter Boys vet Corey Fogelmanis leads the ensemble as Ben, alongside Smile 2 's Miles Gutierrez-Riley as Nathan, Mayfair Witches ' Alexandra Daddario as Hannah, Riverdale 's Cole Sprouse as Thomas and Girls ' Lena Dunham as Ms. Lyons. In looking particularly at the most important element of the novel Dorfman sought to adapt, the writer/director pointed to " the intimacy " of Deaver's source material , describing how reading the book fully immerses readers in Ben's story: Tommy Dorfman: It's written almost like a diary, at times, and that was one of the more challenging things, I think, to bring to screen is, how do we bring that internal experience that you get so vividly through Ben's perspective in a book, and give audiences an opportunity to kind of fly on the wall with them? Be with them over this very specific, concentrated six months of their life? Feeling " most protective " and " most precious " about exploring Ben's emotional rollercoasters, Dorfman found that once she had determined the best way to capture their inner struggles, " everything else came in through that perspective ", with the script then falling into place. Though denoting that " there were 20 versions of this script " before they finally started filming , the majority of that time was her " corseting ", " tightening " and getting the film to " the place of specificity that I think allows for universality and the best performances ". They go on such an emotional roller coaster ride throughout this film. What was it like for you as a performer, really ensuring that you're capturing every little nuance, whether it's a laugh that turns into a cry, like at the party, or just a genuine sense of finding oneself? Corey Fogelmanis: Yeah, I think for me, it was just so important that I was as present as possible. I'd never had the experience of being in every scene of a movie before. So for me, I was just really focused on making sure that I was meeting everybody where they were at, and it kept my energy up. But I think, in a lot of ways, what we were filming kind of mirrored my experience on set. So I remember the first week being very disorienting, and that was when we were shooting the stuff of Ben coming to Hannah's house for the first time. I think I just really tried to trust where I was at, and Tommy did a really wonderful job of letting me know when it was working, and when it wasn't working, and helping me just keep track of everything. So, it was just kind of about trusting. ScreenRant: Alexandra talked a lot about trust, as well, when I just spoke with her, and I love that you were all able to form that trust with one another. I know that this may get you in trouble with one of them, but I would love to hear if, between Lena and Miles, there was anybody whose connection you felt really carried over from off-camera into on-camera for your scenes together? We only had one day with Lena, and I wish it could have been the whole shoot, but I think when Miles came in, he found me on that first day, just kind of really grappling with having this whole world spinning around me, and he was so present, and really met me where I was at, and I really appreciated that. I think that was definitely the basis of Ben and Nathan's relationship, was that care off camera, and it was so spontaneous and wonderful, doing everything with Miles. Alexandra Daddario Got To Explore Her Maternal Instincts Through Her Character Alexandra Daddario's Hannah with her hand on Thomas' chest and smiling at Ben in I Wish You All The Best ScreenRant: I want to talk about Hannah, because she is such a nicely layered character, in that she wants to be this great ally and strong sister, but also has a family that she's trying to raise. Looking at a scene, like after the party, when B comes home late, what is it like finding the balance between all of those layers playing this character throughout the film? Alexandra Daddario: I think it's just like being a mother. I hadn't had a child when we shot this yet, I have one now, and I think I was so on that track, and wanted to be a mother for so long that there was definitely that part of me. I think that's what being a mom is about. It's really about trying to find balance and staying calm and supporting people. Ultimately, when you have younger people in your life, they're going to be on their own paths, and be living their own lives. How do you help guide them, while also allowing them the freedom to go and be who they're going to be? That's what she's taking on, and it's a really beautiful job. ScreenRant: I love the way that really resonates in your and Corey's dynamic on screen. I'd love to hear if that sort of protectiveness also carried over into off-camera, given Corey is still sort of on the rise of late, and you've got some great experience working on everything from blockbusters to indies like this. Alexandra Daddario's Hannah looking sweetly with her hand on Ben's shoulder as they look at a necklace in I Wish You All The Best Alexandra Daddario: I think Corey is an incredibly impressive actor and will do great, great things. I was inspired, because I know how hard it is to be young and to be coming up. It's, again, a journey, it's something you have to go through and figure out on your own. The most important thing you can have is support from people. So, I was really impressed by Tommy's support, and how Tommy and Corey worked together. I think Corey is always going to have people who really, really care and are there to support. ScreenRant: One thing I love is that I Wish You All The Best premiered at South by Southwest back in '24 and has just been getting rave reviews since. It's a little over a year since it made its premiere, but how has it been watching the reception over the course of the past year and a half for this film? Alexandra Daddario: I think it's wonderful. I'm just a small part of the movie, and to be able to be part of it is incredible. But I think it's an important story to tell, and I'm very, very happy that this movie exists, and that people are going to be able to see it. ScreenRant: Did you dive into the novel at all, by the way, for preparation when you were doing this film, or did you really just trust in Tommy? Alexandra Daddario: I did not, actually, this is the first time [I've been asked], I'm embarrassed to say I did not read the novel. But no, I really leaned on Tommy as a director, and her confidence. I felt I really understood the story and understood my character, and we just had a ton of fun. The set was as peaceful as could be. It really allowed all the actors to come together and do great work. So we had a really wonderful time. WhatsApp Share this article on Email Print this article Share this article on Talk Alexandra Daddario gave one of Fforme’s latest designs a Gothic spin at the “I Wish You All the Best’ premiere in New York City on Monday night. “The White Lotus” alum turned to the American luxury brand’s fall 2025 ready-to-wear collection , going Goth in the Mila bias cut long-sleeve dress in black. The dress featured a high, round neckline, with rounded shoulders and extra long sleeves covering Daddario’s hands. Alexandra Daddario Getty Images The bias cut of the dress gave way to a long, flowing maxiskirt. With a loose fit, the dress created an elongated silhouette evocative of a shift or slipdress style. As for accessories, Daddario kept her look minimal, opting for a pair of stud diamond earrings. Her brunette hair featured the controversial side part with soft waves cascading to her shoulders. Makeup for the actress, provided by Shayna Gold, included clean, serene choices, with lightly lined eyes and a glossy lip. Fforme, fall 2025 Giovanni Giannoni/WWD Curated by c reative director Frances Howie , who took over the role from Paul Helbers upon his departure in July 2024, Fforme’s fall 2025 ready-to-wear collection featured “a compelling lineup of modern, sophisticated clothing with artisanal touches at a good price,” Booth Moore wrote in WWD’s review of the collection. Howie pulled from her time working for Alber Elbaz at Lanvin and Stella McCartney to interpret her own iteration on Fforme’s designs. “What I learned from [Alber] was this lightness of touch, which is about the poetry of something remaining a little bit undone,” Howie said, per WWD’s review. Alexandra Daddario Getty Images More recently, Howie debuted Fforme’s spring 2026 ready-to-wear collection during New York Fashion Week in September. Although Fforme hasn’t previously toyed with color, Howie appeared to gradually incorporate some splashes of blues and greens among Fforme’s stock black and white designs. “I Wish You All the Best” follows non-binary teenager Ben DeBacker, played by Corey Fogelmanis, who goes on a journey of self-discovery after they’re kicked out of the house by their parents. The film marks Tommy Dorfman’s directorial debut. “I Wish You All the Best” hits theaters Nov. 7. text: Mayfair Witches Season 2 Gets Netflix Streaming Date Ahead of Season 3 - Comic Book Movies and Superhero Movie News - SuperHeroHype Skip to content Twitter Facebook Instagram Comic Book Movies and Superhero Movie News - SuperHeroHype Open Close Menu Movies TV Comics News Geek Culture Cosplay Videos Forums Search Close Search Photo Credit: AMC News Mayfair Witches Season 2 Gets Netflix Streaming Date Ahead of Season 3 November 18, 2025 By Anubhav Chaudhry AMC’s supernatural series Mayfair Witches has received a new update, outlining when the next season of the Alexandra Daddario show will arrive on Netflix in the United States. The information confirms the show’s continued rollout on the platform following its earlier addition under AMC’s licensing deal. Mayfair Witches Season 2 to stream on Netflix in December Mayfair Witches Season 2 will stream on Netflix US on December 2, 2025. All eight episodes originally aired on AMC between January and March 2025 (via What’s on Netflix ). The series takes place in the Anne Rice “Immortal” universe and follows Rowan Fielding, played by Alexandra Daddario, as she discovers she is the heiress to the Mayfair dynasty. Season 2 expands the cast by adding Alyssa Jirrels, Ben Feldman, Ted Levine, and Mariana A. Novak. Netflix added Season 1 in August 2024 through the AMC–Netflix licensing deal. The renewed agreement brings extra seasons of existing shows and adds new titles like Orphan Black, Echoes, and This Is Going to Hurt. Netflix rolled out Season 1 to select international regions in September 2024. More territories are expected to receive Season 2, with the UK currently planned for March 2026. Netflix will begin releasing Talamasca: The Secret Order in international regions in December 2025 before a later US launch. The Immortal universe continues to grow as productions advance across multiple connected titles. AMC renewed Mayfair Witches for Season 3 and restarted production in Vancouver. Filming is scheduled to wrap on February 11, 2026. The season will explore witchcraft mythology and introduce new “spellbound” families. It will also depict historical events from Salem, Massachusetts. James Frain and Eliza Scanlen have joined the cast. Thomas Schnauz will showrun alongside Esta Spalding. AMC has not announced a release window for Season 3. Netflix availability will depend on the licensing deal, which covers Seasons 1 and 2 through December 2, 2026. Frain will play Solomon and Scanlen will portray Jessica. Details of their roles are under wraps. They join returning stars Alexandra Daddario, Harry Hamlin, Tongayi Chirisa, and Alyssa Jirrels , along with new additions Michiel Huisman (“The Haunting of Hill House”) and Betsy Brandt (“Breaking Bad”). Adapted from Anne Rice ‘s Lives of the Mayfair Witches novel trilogy, the third season of “Mayfair Witches” just started production in Vancouver, Canada. It will dive deeper into the mythology of witchcraft, introduce new ‘spellbound’ families, and feature some of the historical happenings of Salem, MA, the infamous town of witch trials and folklore. Thomas Schnauz (“Breaking Bad,” “Better Call Saul”) has joined as co-showrunner alongside Esta Spalding , who co-created the series with Michelle Ashford . “Mayfair Witches” premiered in 2023 as the second series in AMC’s Anne Rice Immortal Universe following “Interview with the Vampire.” The latest addition, “ Talamasca: The Secret Order ,” kicked off last week. this article on Talk On Monday, Lena Dunham’s pearl-adorned heels commanded the spotlight at the New York premiere of “I Wish You All the Best.” Akin to a piece of art, the shoes were designed by Dauphinette, a New York-based label known for its whimsical, outlandish confections. Debuting on the brand’s fall 2024 runway, the heels were upcycled by Dauphinette’s founder, Olivia Cheng, who explained her affinity with the earth-friendly design practice to luxury resale platform The RealReal. “It’s where I see the greatest opportunity for Dauphinette to make a sustained, lasting impact within the fashion industry and the consumer culture in general,” the designer said. Related Stories Jamie Lee Curtis Puts a Subtle Twist on the Classic Black Pump in London Suki Waterhouse Leans Into Slouchy Boot Trend in Chocolate Leather in New York The actress sourced the shoes from New York-based label Dauphinette. Getty Images The silhouette boasted a nude-colored base intricately embellished with clusters of pearls hanging from the edges, along with one string of pearls that sat across the top of Dunham’s foot. As if that wasn’t eye-catching enough, the pointed toe was decorated with a floral appliqué. You May Also Like The heels debuted on the brand’s fall 2024 runway. Getty Images Giving the pearl heels the spotlight, Dunham dressed in all black. The “Too Much” director teamed a long-sleeve black shirt featuring slit sleeves with a voluminous ankle-length bubble skirt, made from a taffeta fabric. For accessories, she layered a black cord necklace and a silver chain pendant silhouette. Dunham went with a glowy, soft makeup look alongside long, jet-black hair, which was styled in a middle part. “I Wish You All the Best” marks actress Tommy Dorfman’s directorial debut. Hitting theaters on Nov. 7, the movie follows Ben DeBacker (played by Corey Fogelmanis), a high schooler who comes out as nonbinary and is kicked out of their family’s home. Dunham portrays Ms. Lyons, an art teacher who supports Ben at their new school. The film also stars Cole Sprouse, Alexandra Daddario and Lexi Underwood. text: Daddario 'surprised, flattered' at viral 'Wonder Woman' enthusiasm US TODAY’S PAPER | November 27, 2025 | EPAPER ☰ Home Latest Pakistan Business World Sports Opinion Life & Style T-Magazine Blogs Tech Videos Cartoon Home Life & Style Daddario 'surprised, flattered' at viral 'Wonder Woman' enthusiasm Actor says she's open to working with James Gunn but unaware of the online frenzy News Desk November 01, 2025 1 min read facebook twitter whatsup linkded email Alexandra Daddario. Photo: File Alexandra Daddario has finally responded to the viral fan movement casting her as the next Wonder Woman in James Gunn's revamped DC Universe, saying that she is both surprised as well as flattered by the online enthusiasm. The actress addressed the growing speculation during an interview with ScreenRant while promoting her upcoming film' I Wish You All The Best'. "I have to be honest, I haven't seen any of that," Daddario said when asked about the flood of fan art depicting her as Wonder Woman or Catwoman. "I'm flattered to hear that it's happening, but I haven't seen it," the 39-year-old star said, adding that she would love the chance to work with Gunn. "Working with James Gunn would be amazing in any capacity, but I wasn't aware that that was going on." Best known for 'Baywatch', 'The White Lotus', and 'Percy Jackson', Daddario has long been a fan favourite for superhero roles thanks to her striking looks and commanding screen presence. Fans online have been sharing AI renderings and edits showing Daddario in the iconic Amazonian armour, reigniting debate about who could best replace Gal Gadot, who previously played the character in multiple DC films. Gunn confirmed earlier this year that a 'Wonder Woman' project is in active development as part of DCU's 'Chapter One: Gods and Monsters'. A prequel series titled 'Paradise Lost' is also in progress, and while no casting announcements have been made, speculation continues to dominate fan discussions on social media. Online reaction to Daddario's comments was mixed. Some praised her as a natural fit, with one user writing that she "has the look and strength of a true Themysciran warrior." Others were less convinced, arguing that "no one can replace Gal Gadot." Several commenters suggested Daddario might better suit the role of Zatanna or Catwoman instead. As excitement for the DCU's next phase builds, fans remain eager to see if Daddario will take on one of its most iconic roles. With Gunn's team still finalising scripts and casting decisions, her involvement remains purely speculative but the internet's fascination shows no sign of slowing down. facebook twitter whatsup linkded email COMMENTS Replying to X Saved ! Mayfair Witches season 3 is expected to wrap filming in February 2026. Although not much has been revealed about where the story will go, its new location doesn't mean what's been set up previously won't have important repercussions. Season 2 ended with setup for a battle between Rowan and Julian Mayfair (Ted Levine), something season 3 will likely follow up on despite the drastic change to its location. Given Brandt's role as a core character, it seems like Mayfair Witches ' expansion into Salem will have some long-standing repercussions for the show, especially in terms of new faces joining the cast. Now, a Henry Cavill-led thriller from almost a decade ago is rising back to the top of those same charts. Despite its sad 14% on Rotten Tomatoes, it’s nabbed a top spot on Paramount+ this week. Videos by ComicBook.com Night Hunter , also known as Nomis , stars Henry Cavill, Stanley Tucci, Ben Kingsley, and Alexandra Daddario. The plot is tried but true, bordering on trite; Night Hunter focuses on a police task force that traps an online predator, discovering in the process that his crimes are much darker and more intricate than they had expected. Despite a solid cast, the movie comes across as little better than a Cavill-shaped cliche. “You’re going to want to break out your crime cliche bingo card early, lest you miss the full house,” said one reviewer . Read Next Henry Cavill Has 2 Perfect Witcher Replacements Lined Up (but Not a Superman One) It’s Definitely a Mixed Bag Leslie Felperin of the Guardian says, “This is such twaddle it becomes kind of fun, except that there’s an uncomfortable feeling – as with many vigilante movies – that the film is revelling in the sexual violence and covering itself with the fig leaf of justice-seeking.” And that seems to be the consensus of the film—it’s a flashy vigilante flick with no substance behind it and a desire to highlight sexual violence for the sake of it. One critic summed it up perfectly: “As far as you can work out, the film isn’t aiming for slippery Lynchian dream logic or head-scratching dead ends, just stumbling into that arena through sheer confusion.” For a C-rated action movie that would have gone straight to DVD back in the day, the script somehow managed to lure in some really good actors. And it’s not entirely irredeemable, according to some viewers. One said , “This had so much promise and such an amazing cast, but there were so many plot holes and things that were obnoxious with how dumb they were. Like going into buildings with no back up etc. still enjoyed parts of It though after watching It tonight.” Another added , “So bad, yet I still enjoyed it. So much promise in the very first scene, the dread of the girl being chased and her absolute despair and defeat when she drops from the bridge. Pretty good really. I love a lot of the actors here, but the police bits were laughably far fetched. The commissioner instructing his detective to kill the killers? LOL.” What are your thoughts on Night Hunter ? On top of this being a fashion moment worth celebrating, it also highlights another reason to celebrate. That reason is: Isla Fisher is back in the Now You See Me franchise! After not appearing in the sequel, she’s reprising her role as the escape artist Henley Reeves, and I couldn’t be more excited. Based on the Now You See Me: Now You Don’t trailer alone, it seems like everyone is back, and they are on their A-game. There are also a few new magicians played by Justice Smith, Dominic Sessa and Ariana Greenblatt, who I can’t wait to see in action. I’m particularly excited about Henley’s return, though, since she’s my favorite. And after hearing Fisher hilariously roast and compliment her co-star Jesse Eisenberg about getting his magic skills back, I can’t wait to see the original Four Horsemen back in their sassy, sarcastic, and magical form. Co-showrunners Esta Spalding and Thomas Schnauz contribute to the creative direction, supported by Michelle Ashford and Tom Williams. Anne Rice’s Immortal Universe This franchise extends beyond Mayfair Witches. It includes Anne Rice’s Interview with the Vampire, which is currently in production for season three’s adaptation of The Vampire Lestat. Recently, Anne Rice’s Talamasca: The Secret Order premiered, further expanding the universe. The actress says she was 'flattered but unaware' of the viral fancasting By Michael Toledo Published 02 November 2025, 9:49 AM GMT Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on LinkedIn Share on Reddit Share on Flipboard Share on Pocket Alexandra Daddario Alexandra Daddario/Instagram Is she or isn't she the next Wonder Woman? After weeks of fevered speculation, Hollywood star Alexandra Daddario has finally broken her silence on viral rumours linking her to the iconic superhero role in James Gunn's rebooted DC Universe. The White Lotus and Mayfair Witches actress has found herself at the heart of a global fan campaign after social media erupted with fancasts imagining her as the next Diana Prince. Fans across TikTok, X and Reddit have been flooding timelines with digital posters and fan art of Daddario in the Amazonian armour, convinced she is destined to inherit Gal Gadot's crown. But now, Daddario herself has spoken, and her answer may not be what fans were hoping for. How the Hype Began The frenzy began earlier this year when DC Studios boss James Gunn confirmed that Wonder Woman would return in future projects. Almost overnight, fancasts took over the internet, with thousands of fans declaring Daddario their top pick to wield the Lasso of Truth. Her cool, commanding presence and past work in action blockbusters made her an instant favourite, while tags such as #AlexandraDaddarioWonderWoman trended for days. Despite the excitement, DC Studios has yet to make any official casting announcements, keeping fans guessing and fuelling endless online debate. Daddario's Response Speaking to ScreenRant , Daddario addressed the viral speculation head-on, confirming that she has not been approached for the role. 'I have to be honest, I haven't seen any of that [fan art],' she said when asked about the buzz. She added that while she finds the attention flattering, there are no talks taking place. The actress also praised Gunn's creative direction, making clear that she would be open to working with him one day. 'But of course, working with James Gunn would be amazing in any capacity, but I wasn't aware that that was going on,' she added. Her calm and candid response may have cooled the current wave of hysteria, but it has also made fans even more determined to see her in the role. @hayabusa_i.a #cosplay #wonderwoman #dc #alexandradaddario ♬ sonido original - Jeff🧃 Gunn's New DC Vision Since taking over DC Studios in 2023, Gunn has been reshaping the superhero franchise under the banner Chapter One: Gods and Monsters . Confirmed titles include Superman: Legacy , The Brave and the Bold and an untitled Wonder Woman film currently in early development. Industry insiders say a writer originally attached to a Teen Titans project has now joined the Wonder Woman script team. Gunn later clarified that while the film is a priority, it is not being rushed, as the studio wants a strong story before production begins. Why Fans Think She Is the One Fans insist Daddario's mix of strength, grace and on-screen magnetism makes her the perfect fit for Wonder Woman. Her performances in San Andreas , Baywatch and Percy Jackson and the Olympians proved her action credentials, while The White Lotus showcased her emotional depth and charisma. Supporters argue that she embodies the balance of power and compassion that defines Diana Prince, a warrior with humanity. Even without confirmation, the idea of Daddario as Wonder Woman has taken on a life of its own, keeping her name at the centre of every fan wishlist. Life Beyond the Rumours Away from the speculation, Daddario continues to balance stardom with family life . She currently stars as Dr Rowan Fielding in AMC's Mayfair Witches , based on Anne Rice's gothic novels, and welcomed her first child in 2024 with husband Andrew Form, the producer behind A Quiet Place . While fans may still be dreaming of her in the red-and-gold armour, Daddario's poised response proves she does not need a tiara to shine. Hollywood already sees her as a queen in her own right. Advertisement STARRING Bond girl Olga Kurylenko, Other starts impressively enough in a haunting sequence with a masked woman wandering the grounds of an inhospitable estate as alarms go off all round her in the dead of night. Preyed upon by some unknown creature watching her every move, director David Moreau’s latest film reels us in from the off before ultimately tripping over itself after the opening credits have dissipated. Kurylenko gives a stoic performance throughout as Alice, a long-suffering woman who reluctantly returns to her childhood home after the sudden death of her estranged mother. On her arrival, Alice finds the house she left as a teenager, frozen in time, complete with ghosts of the past, and dark and sinister secrets that she must now come face to face with. The high-security system that protects this cheerless mansion is no match for the shadowy presence that calls it home, always one step in front of her, as it perseveres to keep Alice a prisoner in this place filled with unhappy memories. Advertisement Signup for the Limerick Post newsletter Sign Up Despite the Quantum of Solace star’s performance, Other is listless and hugely disappointing. The pacing is as slow as molasses, the scares all predictable and rather scarce, and Moreau, if anything, has opted for style over substance. The creature at the heart of this bleak horror lurks in the darkness for the duration, and regardless of its face-chewing aberrations, it does little to get the pulse racing, or the mind working overtime. In a nutshell, Other is boring. The big reveal in the final scene was obvious from the very beginning and for a man of Moreau’s talents, this is surprisingly all over the place. His last film Mads , was one of the very finest horror films of last year, but sadly, his latest effort is pedestrian and totally forgettable. The Fantastic Four: First Steps recently arrived on Disney+ on November 5. Given that it was the last of the MCU's 2025 movies to both release in theaters and on the streamer, we can now rewatch all of them. Most of the 2025 Marvel movies are among the best MCU films to me. However, that does not mean that rewatching the MCU movies on Disney+ does not bring along some harsh realizations. Pace, story, action, and more elements of the films could have done with some changes — some small, some big. As such, Marvel's upcoming movies could learn a few lessons on how to improve. 10 The Fantastic Four Do Not Use Their Powers Much The Fantastic Four: First Steps is perfect in the way that it adapts the 1960s time period to make a visually distinct and hopeful superhero movie. I loved the Fantastic Four cast and what the movie did with Galactus and the Silver Surfer. That said, for a superhero film, the Fantastic Four entry was light on powers. I believe that might be The Fantastic Four: First Steps ' harshest reality on a rewatch . Reed Richards was barely seen using his stretching powers in comparison to the 2000s Fantastic Four movies. Aside from the Silver Surfer chase and the Galactus fight, their powers — and action scenes — were barely in the film. 9 Taskmaster Should Have Been Used Beyond Shock Value Olga Kurylenko's Antonia Dreykov a.k.a. Taskmaster wears her mask in Thunderbolts* Thunderbolts* tries to establish that anyone can die early on through the death of Olga Kurylenko's Taskmaster. However, rewatching the MCU movie reveals how none of the characters truly feels in any danger of dying after that point. As such, Taskmaster was killed pretty much for nothing , wasting the potential the character still had. Black Widow mostly features Taskmaster as an assassin focused on a mission. The MCU movie's ending set up a future where she could explore what she wanted out of life beyond being a killing machine. However, Thunderbolts* revealed she went back to killing people, now for Valentina Allegra de Fontaine, and died for it. Her death barely impacted the Thunderbolts. 8 The Leader Was A Disappointing Villain Tim Blake Nelson's Samuel Sterns a.k.a. The Leader hides in the shadows in Captain America Brave New World Tim Blake Nelson's Samuel Sterns was teased to become the Leader all the way back in 2008's The Incredible Hulk . As such, his return as the main villain of Captain America: Brave New World was full of promise. Sadly, his potential was not met, with the Leader barely appearing in the MCU movie . His design was underwhelming, with Marvel shying away from a comics-accurate take , and the Leader was played as yet another shadowy villain in a superhero movie. After being absent since 2008 in the MCU, the Leader should have been a more prominent force in his return, but rewatching the fourth Captain America movie cements how disappointing he was. 7 Red Hulk Appeared More In Marketing Than Captain America: Brave New World Harrison Ford looking angry as Red Hulk Captain America Brave New World Captain America: Brave New World ended up including many Hulk elements. Chief among them was Harrison Ford's Thunderbolt Ross, who turned into the Red Hulk near the end of the movie . While that transformation was exciting and his fight with Sam Wilson gave the Captain America movie its boiling point, Red Hulk was barely in the movie. Red Hulk was heavily pushed in Captain America: Brave New World 's trailers. However, he is only in the film for the final fight with Sam. Everyone knew Ross would transform into Red Hulk , so leaving that to happen at the end did not make it more surprising. Instead, the MCU movie could have more heavily connected Red Hulk and the Leader through past experiments. 6 We Still Don't Know Who The MCU's New Avengers Are Sam Wilson looks worn out while standing in a road in Captain America Brave New World The MCU introduced two new Avengers teams in 2025's Marvel movies . We saw one of them in Thunderbolts* , but the New Avengers are unlikely to keep their name due to a legal battle with Captain America's Avengers team. As such, Sam's superhero squad should be the main team of Avengers: Doomsday . However, we got to watch as the Thunderbolts went through great development to become a united superhero team. Sam's Avengers include him and Falcon at the moment, meaning the team will have to debut and bond in Doomsday , which will be packed with other MCU and multiverse characters. We still don't know who Sam's Avengers are, nor did Marvel build a connection with the audience. 5 The Leader's Post-Credits Scene Is Too Vague hulk's nemesis the leader After being defeated by Sam Wilson, who averted his plans of causing a World War, the Leader was imprisoned at the Raft. He came back in Captain America: Brave New World 's post-credits scene. When Sam visits him in prison, the Leader warns him about incoming multiversal threats , which is both vague and makes little sense. Based on what the MCU has shown us, while the Leader is one of Marvel's brightest minds, he has no connection to the multiverse . As such, how would he know about the impending incursions and Secret Wars? The vague tease also left many confused, leading to director Julius Onah claiming he meant the Illuminat i. Upon rewatching the film, that makes even less sense. 4 Sentry May Be Too Powerful Sentry grabs and looks at Bucky Barnes' vibranium arm in Thunderbolts (1) When Sentry was first reported to appear in Thunderbolts* , it became abundantly clear that the team did not have any members powerful enough to go up against the MCU character. Not only did the movie prove that to be true, but rewatching Thunderbolts* and seeing how easily Sentry dispatches Marvel heroes , as well as his The Void side in action, makes him look too powerful. And I don't mean just for Thunderbolts* , which we knew, but for the MCU as a whole. As Sentry, he is essentially DC's Superman with additional powers like telekinesis, heat manipulation, matter manipulation, and more. As The Void, he can turn anyone into a shadow on the pavement and make them relive their darkest fears. Can anyone in the MCU stop him? 3 2025's MCU Movies Are Mostly Good But Their Box Offices Make Sequels Harder Sam Wilson's Captain America in Brave New World looking offscreen Rewatching the MCU's 2025 movies on Disney+ made me realize how I love both Thunderbolts* and The Fantastic Four: First Steps , as well as how Sam Wilson has the potential to lead a better movie than Captain America: Brave New World if Marvel just decides to really focus a movie on him. However, sequels are a hard notion. All three MCU movies underperformed at the box office , with The Fantastic Four: First Steps being the best, amassing $521.9 million. Given how the team only now debuted in the MCU and the Fantastic Four are major heroes, I believe they will get a sequel. However, Sam Wilson's Captain America and the Thunderbolts might not, given their box offices. 2 The Hulk Should Have Appeared In Captain America: Brave New World mcu hulk on gold background from the mcu first 10 years poster set While I wanted to see Sam Wilson stand firmly at the center of Captain America: Brave New World , if Marvel Studios was dead set on having the movie be full of Hulk elements and characters, then it would only have made sense that Mark Ruffalo's Bruce Banner showed up in the film. After all, Hulk's solo movie rights are complicated. The Captain America movie is the closest to a sequel to The Incredible Hulk we might ever get , and we missed the chance of the Hulk interacting with Red Hulk, Liv Tyler's Betty Ross, and Tim Blake Nelson's Leader. Given that Ruffalo will return as the Hulk next year in Spider-Man: Brand New Day , his absence makes even less sense in a rewatch. 1 Doctor Doom Needed More Screen Time Before Avengers: Doomsday Finally, there is a surprising lack of Doctor Doom one year before Robert Downey Jr.'s Victor von Doom becomes the MCU's main villain in Avengers: Doomsday . All 2025 MCU movies set up the next Avengers movie in some form , though Doom only appears in The Fantastic Four: First Steps ' post-credits scene, and Downey's face is not even seen. Given that the franchise was previously setting up Kang the Conqueror as the Multiverse Saga's main villain , I feel Avengers: Doomsday is now left to do a lot of heavy lifting for Doctor Doom in a movie that will be crawling with Marvel characters. 2025's MCU movies could have done a better job of setting up Doom, which becomes notable when rewatching them on Disney+. The Fantastic Four: First Steps recently arrived on Disney+ on November 5. Given that it was the last of the MCU's 2025 movies to both release in theaters and on the streamer, we can now rewatch all of them. Most of the 2025 Marvel movies are among the best MCU films to me. However, that does not mean that rewatching the MCU movies on Disney+ does not bring along some harsh realizations. Pace, story, action, and more elements of the films could have done with some changes — some small, some big. As such, Marvel's upcoming movies could learn a few lessons on how to improve. 10 The Fantastic Four Do Not Use Their Powers Much The Fantastic Four: First Steps is perfect in the way that it adapts the 1960s time period to make a visually distinct and hopeful superhero movie. I loved the Fantastic Four cast and what the movie did with Galactus and the Silver Surfer. That said, for a superhero film, the Fantastic Four entry was light on powers. I believe that might be The Fantastic Four: First Steps ' harshest reality on a rewatch. Reed Richards was barely seen using his stretching powers in comparison to the 2000s Fantastic Four movies. Aside from the Silver Surfer chase and the Galactus fight, their powers — and action scenes — were barely in the film. 9 Taskmaster Should Have Been Used Beyond Shock Value Olga Kurylenko's Antonia Dreykov a. Taskmaster wears her mask in Thunderbolts* Thunderbolts* tries to establish that anyone can die early on through the death of Olga Kurylenko's Taskmaster. However, rewatching the MCU movie reveals how none of the characters truly feels in any danger of dying after that point. As such, Taskmaster was killed pretty much for nothing , wasting the potential the character still had. Black Widow mostly features Taskmaster as an assassin focused on a mission. The MCU movie's ending set up a future where she could explore what she wanted out of life beyond being a killing machine. However, Thunderbolts* revealed she went back to killing people, now for Valentina Allegra de Fontaine, and died for it. Her death barely impacted the Thunderbolts. 8 The Leader Was A Disappointing Villain Tim Blake Nelson's Samuel Sterns a. The Leader hides in the shadows in Captain America Brave New World Tim Blake Nelson's Samuel Sterns was teased to become the Leader all the way back in 2008's The Incredible Hulk. As such, his return as the main villain of Captain America: Brave New World was full of promise. Sadly, his potential was not met, with the Leader barely appearing in the MCU movie. His design was underwhelming, with Marvel shying away from a comics-accurate take , and the Leader was played as yet another shadowy villain in a superhero movie. After being absent since 2008 in the MCU, the Leader should have been a more prominent force in his return, but rewatching the fourth Captain America movie cements how disappointing he was. 7 Red Hulk Appeared More In Marketing Than Captain America: Brave New World Harrison Ford looking angry as Red Hulk Captain America Brave New World Captain America: Brave New World ended up including many Hulk elements. Chief among them was Harrison Ford's Thunderbolt Ross, who turned into the Red Hulk near the end of the movie. While that transformation was exciting and his fight with Sam Wilson gave the Captain America movie its boiling point, Red Hulk was barely in the movie. Red Hulk was heavily pushed in Captain America: Brave New World 's trailers. However, he is only in the film for the final fight with Sam. Everyone knew Ross would transform into Red Hulk , so leaving that to happen at the end did not make it more surprising. Instead, the MCU movie could have more heavily connected Red Hulk and the Leader through past experiments. 6 We Still Don't Know Who The MCU's New Avengers Are Sam Wilson looks worn out while standing in a road in Captain America Brave New World The MCU introduced two new Avengers teams in 2025's Marvel movies. We saw one of them in Thunderbolts* , but the New Avengers are unlikely to keep their name due to a legal battle with Captain America's Avengers team. As such, Sam's superhero squad should be the main team of Avengers: Doomsday. However, we got to watch as the Thunderbolts went through great development to become a united superhero team. Sam's Avengers include him and Falcon at the moment, meaning the team will have to debut and bond in Doomsday , which will be packed with other MCU and multiverse characters. We still don't know who Sam's Avengers are, nor did Marvel build a connection with the audience. 5 The Leader's Post-Credits Scene Is Too Vague hulk's nemesis the leader After being defeated by Sam Wilson, who averted his plans of causing a World War, the Leader was imprisoned at the Raft. He came back in Captain America: Brave New World 's post-credits scene. When Sam visits him in prison, the Leader warns him about incoming multiversal threats , which is both vague and makes little sense. Based on what the MCU has shown us, while the Leader is one of Marvel's brightest minds, he has no connection to the multiverse. As such, how would he know about the impending incursions and Secret Wars? The vague tease also left many confused, leading to director Julius Onah claiming he meant the Illuminat i. Upon rewatching the film, that makes even less sense. 4 Sentry May Be Too Powerful Sentry grabs and looks at Bucky Barnes' vibranium arm in Thunderbolts (1) When Sentry was first reported to appear in Thunderbolts* , it became abundantly clear that the team did not have any members powerful enough to go up against the MCU character. Not only did the movie prove that to be true, but rewatching Thunderbolts* and seeing how easily Sentry dispatches Marvel heroes , as well as his The Void side in action, makes him look too powerful. And I don't mean just for Thunderbolts* , which we knew, but for the MCU as a whole. As Sentry, he is essentially DC's Superman with additional powers like telekinesis, heat manipulation, matter manipulation, and more. As The Void, he can turn anyone into a shadow on the pavement and make them relive their darkest fears. Can anyone in the MCU stop him? 3 2025's MCU Movies Are Mostly Good But Their Box Offices Make Sequels Harder Sam Wilson's Captain America in Brave New World looking offscreen Rewatching the MCU's 2025 movies on Disney+ made me realize how I love both Thunderbolts* and The Fantastic Four: First Steps , as well as how Sam Wilson has the potential to lead a better movie than Captain America: Brave New World if Marvel just decides to really focus a movie on him. However, sequels are a hard notion. All three MCU movies underperformed at the box office , with The Fantastic Four: First Steps being the best, amassing $521. Given how the team only now debuted in the MCU and the Fantastic Four are major heroes, I believe they will get a sequel. However, Sam Wilson's Captain America and the Thunderbolts might not, given their box offices. 2 The Hulk Should Have Appeared In Captain America: Brave New World mcu hulk on gold background from the mcu first 10 years poster set While I wanted to see Sam Wilson stand firmly at the center of Captain America: Brave New World , if Marvel Studios was dead set on having the movie be full of Hulk elements and characters, then it would only have made sense that Mark Ruffalo's Bruce Banner showed up in the film. After all, Hulk's solo movie rights are complicated. The Captain America movie is the closest to a sequel to The Incredible Hulk we might ever get , and we missed the chance of the Hulk interacting with Red Hulk, Liv Tyler's Betty Ross, and Tim Blake Nelson's Leader. Given that Ruffalo will return as the Hulk next year in Spider-Man: Brand New Day , his absence makes even less sense in a rewatch. 1 Doctor Doom Needed More Screen Time Before Avengers: Doomsday Finally, there is a surprising lack of Doctor Doom one year before Robert Downey Jr. 's Victor von Doom becomes the MCU's main villain in Avengers: Doomsday. All 2025 MCU movies set up the next Avengers movie in some form , though Doom only appears in The Fantastic Four: First Steps ' post-credits scene, and Downey's face is not even seen. Given that the franchise was previously setting up Kang the Conqueror as the Multiverse Saga's main villain , I feel Avengers: Doomsday is now left to do a lot of heavy lifting for Doctor Doom in a movie that will be crawling with Marvel characters. 2025's MCU movies could have done a better job of setting up Doom, which becomes notable when rewatching them on Disney+. GL and BL (Boys’ Love) series, which center on same-sex romantic relationships, have become a popular genre across Asia, with Thailand emerging as a major production hub for such content. Related Stories 'Smallville' Star Allison Mack Gives First Interview on Surviving the Abusive Sex Cult NXIVM and Going to Prison: 'I Don't See Myself as Innocent' Allison Mack Reunites With 'Smallville' Co-Star Michael Rosenbaum to Detail 'Insidious' NXIVM Cult, Reveals Keith Raniere Sent Her a Letter Under the arrangement, Cappu Films and VelCurve Studio — the production company behind the sci-fi film “Uranus 2324” — will jointly handle international sales for Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam, North America, Latin America and Singapore. Helmed by Fuse Kittisak Cheewasatjasakun, the series follows two female architects, portrayed by Kao Supassara Thanachart and Jane Methika Jiranorraphat, whose romantic relationship deteriorates into professional animosity after one uses the other’s designs in a competition without permission. Popular on Variety The show debuted Oct. 2 with weekly Thursday releases. Thailand’s Channel 3 is airing an eight-episode version, while Tencent’s WeTV platform carries an extended cut with 10 episodes. Fan events for the final two episodes are planned for early December 2025. Keetawat Chinnakote, CEO and executive producer at VelCurve Studio, and Janice Woo, founder and head of sales at Cappu Films, negotiated the agreement. “‘Love Design’ is a GL series that tells the story of the architecture profession — exploring both the challenges of work and the romantic relationships of its characters,” said Keetawat. “It stars the talented Kao Supassara and Jane Methika, alongside promising newcomers Friend Tofan and Palm Paramee. Produced by VelCurve Studio, the series is crafted with a strong commitment to high production standards and storytelling that allows global audiences to easily understand and connect with its context and emotions.” He characterized the series as Thai soft power content that showcases the country’s creative capabilities internationally, noting his hopes for global audience support through the Cappu Films partnership. “At Cappu Films, we are passionate about bringing distinctive Asian stories with global resonance to audiences worldwide,” said Woo. “‘Love Design’ is a bold and emotionally layered GL series that combines romance, rivalry, and ambition in a fresh way. Partnering with VelCurve Studio allows us to champion diverse storytelling while tapping into the phenomenal energy of the GL fan community across Asia and beyond.” Cappu Films handles international sales for emerging directors and commercial genre content. The company’s TCCF slate features the Busan Vision competition winner “Malika” from Kazakhstan, the action-thriller “Fox Hunt” with Tony Leung Chiu-wai and Olga Kurylenko, Josh Radnor’s “All Happy Families,” the Karlovy Vary entry “Promise, I’ll Be Fine” from Aerofilms/Filmtopia, and the Chinese action title “Assassin,” which Film Movement’s Omnibus Entertainment label will distribute in North America. VelCurve Studio’s previous work includes “Uranus 2324,” which Netflix acquired for its streaming service throughout Southeast Asia, covering Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Brunei, Cambodia, Laos, East Timor, Vietnam, the Philippines, Myanmar and Indonesia. GL and BL (Boys’ Love) series, which center on same-sex romantic relationships, have become a popular genre across Asia, with Thailand emerging as a major production hub for such content. Helmed by Fuse Kittisak Cheewasatjasakun, the series follows two female architects, portrayed by Kao Supassara Thanachart and Jane Methika Jiranorraphat, whose romantic relationship deteriorates into professional animosity after one uses the other’s designs in a competition without permission. Popular on Variety The show debuted Oct. 2 with weekly Thursday releases. Thailand’s Channel 3 is airing an eight-episode version, while Tencent’s WeTV platform carries an extended cut with 10 episodes. Fan events for the final two episodes are planned for early December 2025. Keetawat Chinnakote, CEO and executive producer at VelCurve Studio, and Janice Woo, founder and head of sales at Cappu Films, negotiated the agreement. “‘Love Design’ is a GL series that tells the story of the architecture profession — exploring both the challenges of work and the romantic relationships of its characters,” said Keetawat. “It stars the talented Kao Supassara and Jane Methika, alongside promising newcomers Friend Tofan and Palm Paramee. Partnering with VelCurve Studio allows us to champion diverse storytelling while tapping into the phenomenal energy of the GL fan community across Asia and beyond.” Cappu Films handles international sales for emerging directors and commercial genre content. His passion for all things entertainment related has led him to dissect movies and television for publications such as The Escapist , DiscussingFilm , SlashFilm , ComicBook , and Full Circle Cinema. Sign in to your MovieWeb account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Marvel Studios has developed a reputation in recent years for releasing films that have been less stellar than they once were. Due to the large number of projects that the studio churns out every year, this inevitably leads to a drop-off in quality, and not just in terms of thematic content or story. Rather, the MCU has been criticized for its excessive use of CGI, especially in ways that don't look as immersive or realistic as they once did. One of the best-reviewed MCU movies in recent memory, Thunderbolts* , has now itself been the subject of scrutiny for its visual effects. The Corridor Crew YouTube channel uploaded a video that broke down the use of CGI in Thunderbolts* , the MCU film released earlier this year, directed by Jake Schreier. The group watched various clips from the film and criticized the odd choices that went into the use of CGI, both in subtle and more obvious ways. One such instance is the fight in the vault at the beginning of the film, which sees the likes of Yelena (Florence Pugh), John Walker (Wyatt Russell), Ghost (Hannah John Kamen), and Taskmaster (Olga Kurylenko) battle one another. One member of the Corridor Crew, Niko, commented on the fight, saying that he's "not trying to be mean, because also, this is way better than anything I could do. But it's kind of janky." Specifically, the moment where Taskmaster is punched and sent flying by John Walker is what bothers the crew the most, with Wren saying, "The stunt pulls and stuff like that have a weird motion. The motion gets me on this... When you get hit, you should get thrown backwards immediately... Not accelerate." Despite "Janky" CGI, 'Thunderbolts' Is a Step in the Right Direction Disney Jordan of the Corridor Crew provided some interesting commentary of his own on the fight, saying that the odd look this action sequence has is representative of a larger problem with the post-production process. "This is kind of the downside of being able to fix anything in post... Visual effects houses are so good these days, that they can bridge a lot of those gaps. But there are still shots like this where something is off, that something's a little wrong," Jordan stated. Several filmmakers have commented on the somewhat unorthodox production process of Marvel Studios projects. There has been commentary by several actors, some who have even recently done work on Avengers: Doomsday , about the idea that their work, done in isolation, is edited together using CGI and visual effects at a later date. Still, Thunderbolts* feels like one of the less extreme examples of this practice, as Schreier's film places much more emphasis on character work and drama than the larger-than-life superhero fights. The film, while struggling at the box office by MCU standards, still received positive reviews. Although there are apparently problems with the CG work, the movie is a step in the right direction. 3 /5 Thunderbolts* Like Follow Followed PG-13 Action Science Fiction Adventure Release Date May 2, 2025 Runtime 127 minutes Director Jake Schreier Writers Eric Pearson, Joanna Calo Producers Kevin Feige Franchise(s) Marvel Cinematic Universe Cast See All Florence Pugh Yelena Belova Sebastian Stan Bucky Barnes Where to watch Close WHERE TO WATCH Streaming RENT BUY Genres Action , Science Fiction , Adventure Powered by Expand Collapse Google is updating how content is shown. The supermodel, who turned 30 last month, recently revealed plans to quit modeling for a drastically different new career. With her 818 Tequila brand already well-established and a modelling resume off the charts, it's no surprise Kendall may be wanting to dip her toes in a new industry. Since becoming the frontrunner, Kendall's mother Kris Jenner pulled off an epic 007-themed birthday bash, where Kendall channeled her inner Bond Girl in a ruby red gown. Her sister Kim, meanwhile, wore a very similar dress to what Halle sported in the 2002 movie Die Another Day. Halle, 59, memorably wore the risqué frock when meeting James Bond face-to-face at a swanky party. Kendall Jenner, who channelled Caterina Murino in Casino Royale at her mum Kris' 007-themed bash at the weekend, has emerged as bookies' favourite to be cast as the next Bond Girl Kim, whose series All's Fair has received scathing reviews , modeled almost an exact same version of the lavender dress, complete with the low-cut back. Kendall showed she already has that 'Bond look' and proved she was personally a fan of the franchise when she channeled actress Ursula in a tiny white bikini in 2019. She showed off her statuesque frame as she sauntered across the beach, calling to mind the 1962 film's famous Bond girl moment. Brand and Culture Expert Nick Ede told Daily Mail that casting the supermodel will be a 'brilliant and modern move' in bringing a whole new generation of fans to the much-loved franchise. He said: ' To cast her in the new franchise would be a brilliant and very modern move. 'She fits the mould of the classic Bond woman, effortlessly glamorous, poised, and mysterious but she also brings a more current edge that could completely redefine the role and take away from the stereotype we've become accustomed to. 'What makes Kendall so interesting is that she’s not just a model she’s a brand in herself. 'Turning 30 marks a new chapter, and with her success in business with her 818 Tequila and her growing confidence on screen, she’s clearly looking to evolve. The timing couldn’t be better. 'For Kendall this could be a chance for her to prove she’s more than just a reality star model turned business mogul, and to step into an iconic cinematic legacy with her own twist of glamour.' He added Kendall is a natural successor to models and former Bond Girls like Ursula Andress, Grace Jones and Olga Kurylenko. Bookmaker Coral has made Kendall the odds-on favourite at 1/2. Also in the running for the part are Sydney Sweeney ( 2/1), Cara Delevingne (5/1) and Margot Robbie (6/1). On Kendall potentially copying her sister Kim in the world of acting, Nick added: 'She's appeared in adverts and don’t forget she's been on our screens since she was 11 as a reality star so she knows all the right angles and she also knows how to be directed too. 'She may even give her sister Kim a run for her money and outshine her reviews for All's Fair! Which wont be hard!' The most recent release in the film franchise was the 2021 movie No Time to Die, which marked the final performance from Daniel Craig in the legendary role of the secret agent. Craig, 57, told The Sunday Times last year about the impact the role, which he played across five feature films from 2006 thru 2021, had on his career as a whole. 'I was becoming a star, whatever that means, and people wanted me in their films. Incredible.' He added, 'Most actors are out of work for large chunks so you take your job offers - but they left me empty. Then, bottom line, I got paid. 'I was so exhausted at the end of a Bond it would take me six months to recover emotionally. I always had the attitude that life must come first and, when work came first for a while, it strung me out.' text: Best Superhero Movies of 2025 (So Far) - Comic Book Movies and Superhero Movie News - SuperHeroHype Skip to content Twitter Facebook Instagram Comic Book Movies and Superhero Movie News - SuperHeroHype Open Close Menu Movies TV Comics News Geek Culture Cosplay Videos Forums Search Close Search Features Best Superhero Movies of 2025 (So Far) November 12, 2025 By Erin Boswell After a somewhat rough 2024 for the genre, 2025 has bounced back and been a great year for superhero movies . While the last few years saw superhero films start to feel repetitive and a bit stale, this year managed to shake off the fatigue with a lineup that reminded us why we fell in love with the genre in the first place. Here are the best superhero movies of 2025. What are the best superhero movies of 2025? Though there haven’t been too many official releases from DC or the MCU , that’s not a bad thing. As the saying goes, less is more. Still, we got a surprisingly strong and varied lineup: from James Gunn’s long-awaited Superman, to a fantastically Fantastic Four, a new Captain America featuring the franchise’s new lead, the gritty Thunderbolts*, and an unassuming animated superhero film that shattered box office records, grossing over $2 billion to become the highest-earning film of the year. Ne Zha 2 Written and directed by Jiaozi, Ne Zha 2 is a kid-friendly animated Chinese film that leans just enough into the mythological to count as much of a superhero movie as a fantasy one. It’s the sequel to Ne Zha, released in 2019, which already had a big following and proved that international audiences were more than ready for a different kind of animated hero. But following up a hit like that isn’t easy. Did it pull it off? A resounding yes . This time around, we pick up with the rebellious boy Ne Zha, born of mortal parents feared by the gods. When a dark force begins upsetting the balance of the heavens, Ne Zha is forced to confront both powerful enemies and his own inner turmoil as the chosen protector of humankind. While the movie has plenty of action-packed adventure and battle sequences, it still finds grounding in the character relationships and the importance of friends and family. Expect a bit of immortal potty humor in this one — it is a movie about a superpowered kid after all. Buy it on Amazon Captain America: Brave New World Maybe the least well-received of our superhero movie picks, Captain America: Brave New World marks the fourth Captain America standalone in the Marvel lineup. People are still going to see it, and the gross alone is enough to prove it. Brave New World took in $415 million globally, showing it’s still a character we care about, especially when you give him a new story with a new actor. This time, Anthony Mackie officially steps into the role as the new Captain America, taking up the shield as Sam Wilson. This change has been in the works since The Falcon and the Winter Soldier. Brave New World follows Sam as he navigates his new responsibilities as a global symbol (those are some big boots to step into) while uncovering a conspiracy within the government he’s sworn to serve. We get old allies and new enemies, including Harrison Ford stepping into the role of President Thaddeus “Thunderbolt” Ross (replacing the late William Hurt). Ross has his own ideas about how superheroes should be managed, putting him directly at odds with Sam’s sense of freedom and accountability. Blending political thriller vibes within the MCU action style, Brave New World is worth a watch even if it doesn’t completely hit the mark. Critics mostly ripped this one apart, but audience response was generally favorable. Buy it on Amazon The Fantastic Four: First Steps One of the most favorably rated superhero movies of the year, The Fantastic Four: First Steps, is a full-blown redemption story. We’re not just talking about the characters, but about the franchise itself. After the 2015 reboot was a dismal misfire, Marvel finally got their hands on the property and gave us a version that works. It’s the first Fantastic Four film set within the MCU, and the difference is clear. First Steps takes us into a 1960s retro-future world and follows Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal), Sue Storm (Vanessa Kirby), Johnny Storm (Joseph Quinn), and Ben Grimm (Ebon Moss-Bachrach) as they gain their powers after a space expedition goes wrong. We quickly make it through a montage-exposition that doesn’t leave us wanting. Then, we’re right into the confrontation with the Silver Surfer (played by Julia Garner). While there’s plenty of adventure, the film really works thanks to its character writing. Unlike the ensemble dynamics often seen in other MCU films, this has a really touching element: every character has at least one meaty scene with another teammate. You can read more about that in Superherohype’s review here. But beyond the character-driven storytelling, The Fantastic Four: First Steps also delivers some of Marvel’s best visual effects in years. Buy it on Amazon Thunderbolts* What works about Thunderbolts* is that it’s not trying to be just another lineup in the MCU canon; instead, it rejects what hasn’t been working in the Marvel superhero universe lately and shakes things up. Thunderbolts* works somewhat like Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 1, bringing a found-family comedy energy to the franchise. Here, we’ve got the MCU’s version of a team-up movie where the heroes are all, technically, former villains or antiheroes. The story brings together an unconventional team that includes Yelena Belova (Florence Pugh), Bucky Barnes (Sebastian Stan), Red Guardian (David Harbour), Taskmaster (Olga Kurylenko), and John Walker a.k.a. U.S. Agent (Wyatt Russell), under the direction of Valentina Allegra de Fontaine, played by Julia Louis-Dreyfus . That casting choice in itself is a unique take on a villain. We can definitely see what would happen if Veep’s Selina Meyer went to the dark side. Oh, and Bob. We can’t forget Bob (Lewis Pullman). After the team gets caught in a setup designed to wipe them out, they’re forced to band together to take on a new wave of villainous machinations — while also confronting the ghosts of their own pasts. Buy it on Amazon Superman Maybe the most anticipated film in the superhero lineup, Superman had the potential to be an utter letdown. But we put our trust in James Gunn, and it didn’t disappoint. Some naysayers will have a different opinion, but for the first film in the DC Universe, Superman is an entertaining ride from start to finish. The movie doesn’t start with the origin story we’ve all seen a hundred times. This time around, Superman is already established but has been having a rough go of it lately, which we won’t expand on here. Instead, the first scene drops us into a very beat-up Superman (David Corenswet) stranded in the arctic landscape of Krypton, in desperate need of help and calling on his superhero dog, Krypto, to save the day. It’s a confusing, hilarious mix-up that no one saw coming, and it perfectly sets the tone for the kind of movie we’re in for. Nothing is off-limits here, and we’re just along for whatever comes next. You can read more on the film here. Buy it on Amazon How we picked the best superhero movies of 2025 (so far) There weren’t too many superhero films to pick from this year, though we could have added a few other contenders for superheroic movies, if not strictly superhero movies. While the last few years saw superhero films start to feel repetitive and a bit stale, this year managed to shake off the fatigue with a lineup that reminded us why we fell in love with the genre in the first place. Here are the best superhero movies of 2025. What are the best superhero movies of 2025? Though there haven’t been too many official releases from DC or the MCU , that’s not a bad thing. As the saying goes, less is more. Still, we got a surprisingly strong and varied lineup: from James Gunn’s long-awaited Superman, to a fantastically Fantastic Four, a new Captain America featuring the franchise’s new lead, the gritty Thunderbolts*, and an unassuming animated superhero film that shattered box office records, grossing over $2 billion to become the highest-earning film of the year. Ne Zha 2 Written and directed by Jiaozi, Ne Zha 2 is a kid-friendly animated Chinese film that leans just enough into the mythological to count as much of a superhero movie as a fantasy one. It’s the sequel to Ne Zha, released in 2019, which already had a big following and proved that international audiences were more than ready for a different kind of animated hero. But following up a hit like that isn’t easy. Did it pull it off? A resounding yes. This time around, we pick up with the rebellious boy Ne Zha, born of mortal parents feared by the gods. When a dark force begins upsetting the balance of the heavens, Ne Zha is forced to confront both powerful enemies and his own inner turmoil as the chosen protector of humankind. While the movie has plenty of action-packed adventure and battle sequences, it still finds grounding in the character relationships and the importance of friends and family. Expect a bit of immortal potty humor in this one — it is a movie about a superpowered kid after all. Buy it on Amazon Captain America: Brave New World Maybe the least well-received of our superhero movie picks, Captain America: Brave New World marks the fourth Captain America standalone in the Marvel lineup. People are still going to see it, and the gross alone is enough to prove it. Brave New World took in $415 million globally, showing it’s still a character we care about, especially when you give him a new story with a new actor. This time, Anthony Mackie officially steps into the role as the new Captain America, taking up the shield as Sam Wilson. This change has been in the works since The Falcon and the Winter Soldier. Brave New World follows Sam as he navigates his new responsibilities as a global symbol (those are some big boots to step into) while uncovering a conspiracy within the government he’s sworn to serve. We get old allies and new enemies, including Harrison Ford stepping into the role of President Thaddeus “Thunderbolt” Ross (replacing the late William Hurt). Ross has his own ideas about how superheroes should be managed, putting him directly at odds with Sam’s sense of freedom and accountability. Blending political thriller vibes within the MCU action style, Brave New World is worth a watch even if it doesn’t completely hit the mark. Critics mostly ripped this one apart, but audience response was generally favorable. Buy it on Amazon The Fantastic Four: First Steps One of the most favorably rated superhero movies of the year, The Fantastic Four: First Steps, is a full-blown redemption story. We’re not just talking about the characters, but about the franchise itself. After the 2015 reboot was a dismal misfire, Marvel finally got their hands on the property and gave us a version that works. It’s the first Fantastic Four film set within the MCU, and the difference is clear. First Steps takes us into a 1960s retro-future world and follows Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal), Sue Storm (Vanessa Kirby), Johnny Storm (Joseph Quinn), and Ben Grimm (Ebon Moss-Bachrach) as they gain their powers after a space expedition goes wrong. We quickly make it through a montage-exposition that doesn’t leave us wanting. Then, we’re right into the confrontation with the Silver Surfer (played by Julia Garner). While there’s plenty of adventure, the film really works thanks to its character writing. Unlike the ensemble dynamics often seen in other MCU films, this has a really touching element: every character has at least one meaty scene with another teammate. You can read more about that in Superherohype’s review here. But beyond the character-driven storytelling, The Fantastic Four: First Steps also delivers some of Marvel’s best visual effects in years. Buy it on Amazon Thunderbolts* What works about Thunderbolts* is that it’s not trying to be just another lineup in the MCU canon; instead, it rejects what hasn’t been working in the Marvel superhero universe lately and shakes things up. Thunderbolts* works somewhat like Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 1, bringing a found-family comedy energy to the franchise. Here, we’ve got the MCU’s version of a team-up movie where the heroes are all, technically, former villains or antiheroes. The story brings together an unconventional team that includes Yelena Belova (Florence Pugh), Bucky Barnes (Sebastian Stan), Red Guardian (David Harbour), Taskmaster (Olga Kurylenko), and John Walker a. Agent (Wyatt Russell), under the direction of Valentina Allegra de Fontaine, played by Julia Louis-Dreyfus. That casting choice in itself is a unique take on a villain. We can definitely see what would happen if Veep’s Selina Meyer went to the dark side. We can’t forget Bob (Lewis Pullman). After the team gets caught in a setup designed to wipe them out, they’re forced to band together to take on a new wave of villainous machinations — while also confronting the ghosts of their own pasts. Buy it on Amazon Superman Maybe the most anticipated film in the superhero lineup, Superman had the potential to be an utter letdown. But we put our trust in James Gunn, and it didn’t disappoint. Some naysayers will have a different opinion, but for the first film in the DC Universe, Superman is an entertaining ride from start to finish. The movie doesn’t start with the origin story we’ve all seen a hundred times. This time around, Superman is already established but has been having a rough go of it lately, which we won’t expand on here. Instead, the first scene drops us into a very beat-up Superman (David Corenswet) stranded in the arctic landscape of Krypton, in desperate need of help and calling on his superhero dog, Krypto, to save the day. It’s a confusing, hilarious mix-up that no one saw coming, and it perfectly sets the tone for the kind of movie we’re in for. Nothing is off-limits here, and we’re just along for whatever comes next. You can read more on the film here. To narrow down our choices, we looked at the films with the best audience and fan feedback, the ones shaking up the genre, and the movies we genuinely had the most fun watching. text: Celebrity babies born in 2025: Hollywood stars who embraced parenthood Home latest pakistan world sports showbiz entertainment Royal Hollywood business health Sci-Tech Food Fact Check big picture Videos shows Watch LIVE TV X Home Latest Pakistan World Sports Showbiz Fact Check big picture Videos Shows LIVE TV Home Entertainment Celebrity babies born in 2025: Hollywood stars who embraced parenthood Jennifer Lawrence, Lily Collins and others welcome kids this year By Geo News Digital Desk | November 25, 2025 Jennifer Lawrence, Lily Collins and others welcome kids this year The year 2025 is shaping up to be a landmark year for celebrity baby news, with Hollywood’s brightest stars welcoming new additions and others announcing long-awaited pregnancies. From giving birth, to adopting and welcoming children through surrogacy, many A-list celebrities in Hollywood embraced parenthood this year. Here is a list of stars who welcomed their little sunshines in 2025. Rihanna and A$AP Rocky: The Diamonds singer welcomed a baby with partner A$AP Rocky on September 13, 2025, who they named as Rocki Irish Mayers. The two announced the birth of their newly born child on Instagram with a photo of their little bundle of joy and a pair of pink boxing gloves. The couple already share two sons RZA and Riot. Meghan Fox and Machine Gun Kelly: Meghan Fox gave birth to a baby girl in March 2025 with ex-fiancé Machine Gun Kelly. The model previously shares three sons namely Noah, Bodhi and Journey with former partner Brian Austin Green Lily Collins and Charlie McDowell: The Emily in Paris famed Lily Collins welcomed a daughter named Tove Jane McDowell on January 31, 2025, with husband Charlie McDowell via surrogacy. Jennifer Lawrence and Cooke Maroney: Jennifer Lawrence, who already shares a son named Cy with husband Cook Maroney, gave birth to their second baby in the early 2025. She has kept the name of her second child secret. However, a keychain named Louie was spotted, which eagle-eyed fans think might be the name. Chris Evans and Alba Baptista: Chris Evans and Alba Baptista tied the knot in September 2023 after sparking romance rumours in 2022. In October, the lovebirds welcomed their first child to the world. Henry Cavill and Natalia Viscuso: Henry Cavill and his girlfriend Natalie Viscuso share one child together a daughter, who was born in early 2025. The Man of Steel actor kept the exact date of birth and name private; however, he confirmed the gender of his baby in an interview with British GQ. Cardi B and Stefon Diggs: Cardi B, Grammy Award winner, welcomed a baby with American footballer Stefon Diggs on November 13. Cardi is already a mom to three children Kulture, Wave and Blossom which she shares with her ex Offset. Millie Bobby Brown and Jake Bongiovi: The Stranger Things star Millie Bobby Brown tied the knot with Jake Bongiovi in 2024. One year after their marriage, the couple announced that they became parents to little child through adoption. Tom Hiddleston and Zawe Ashton: Loki star Tom Hiddleston and his fiancé Zawe Ashton, who already share a child, welcomed their second baby in November 2025. The duo has kept the names and gender of their children private.
